France to deploy 70,000 police for fresh weekend protests
items.description: France will deploy about 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests on Saturday after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago. Protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living. About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a news conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen as the frontrunner and indicating her position has been strengthened by the latest events. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is due at the weekend to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected and local authorities fearing clashes as counter-protesters also head to the city south of Paris. Macron met representatives of secondary school pupils on Friday, but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands. Offenders jailed Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday. Courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend. An extreme-left group in western France posted on its website a call for its supporters to be “uncatchable, unpredictable, to evade the deployment” of police. Protest restrictions Authorities have stepped up security measures and imposed restrictions on protests. In Orleans, between 20,000 and 30,000 people are expected to come out against Le Pen’s National Rally party, but the gathering will be barred from the city centre, the prefecture said. In the southeastern city of Lyon, central areas will also be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend. In Paris, police overturned a previous permit for union-led protesters to march between Bastille and Nation squares in the east. The force said the parade could instead go in the afternoon along an alternative route on the southeastern edge of the city. Unions vowed to push ahead on the banned route, citing safety concerns over the alternative. Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis” – the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department. In the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short. Police ‘responsibility’ The restrictions, including outright bans on protests in some cities, have drawn criticism. Amnesty International denounced what it called “a slide toward authoritarian practice”, saying the measures were “jeopardising the right to demonstrate peacefully”. About 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend following questions over police preparedness and intelligence gathering ahead of last week’s violence. “Police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch. She voiced alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons during recent gatherings. The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors. A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections. It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on about 70 percent of the vote.

items.title: Nigerian woman jailed seven years for human trafficking in Tamale
items.description: A 24-year-old Nigerian woman has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment with hard labour for human trafficking after a trial at the Gender-Based Violence Court in Tamale. Mariam Yussif was convicted on October 22, 2026, following a police investigation into the alleged recruitment and movement of victims from Nigeria to Ghana for sexual exploitation. The Northern Regional Police Command said Yussif and her 22-year-old sister, Precious Clement, were arrested at Yendi on August 17, 2026, over their alleged involvement in the operation. Yussif was subsequently charged under Section 2(1) of the Human Trafficking Act, 2005 (Act 694), and appeared before the court on August 19. She pleaded not guilty and was remanded into custody while the case proceeded. After several adjournments, the court concluded the trial and found her guilty, leading to the custodial sentence. She has since been transferred to Tamale Central Prison to begin serving her term. Sister released, victims reunited with families The police said no case was established against Clement, who was released. The two victims connected to the case have also been repatriated to Nigeria and reunited with their respective families. The outcome brings the prosecution to a close against Yussif, while the release of her sister underscores the need for individual responsibility to be established through evidence in trafficking investigations. The Northern Regional Police Command said the conviction demonstrated the importance of intelligence-led operations, thorough investigations and effective prosecution in tackling human trafficking. It urged members of the public to report suspected trafficking cases to the appropriate authorities, reaffirming its commitment to protecting vulnerable people and pursuing those involved in the crime. Human trafficking involves the recruitment, movement or receipt of people through prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. Sexual exploitation is one of the forms of abuse traffickers may seek to facilitate. The police have encouraged the public to remain alert to suspected cases and provide information that could help law enforcement agencies intervene and protect potential victims.

items.title: À une semaine des élections de mi-mandat, Obama s’engage dans la campagne
items.description: L’ancien président démocrate se rendra à Cleveland aujourd’hui, samedi 24, aux côtés d’Amy Acton, candidate au poste de gouverneure de l’État, et de Sherrod Brown, candidat au Sénat, qui se présente contre le républicain Jon Husted. Celui-ci avait été nommé en janvier 2025 par le gouverneur Mike DeWine en remplacement de J.D. Vance. Obama tiendra ensuite à Détroit un meeting de soutien à Abdul El-Sayed, candidat au Sénat face au républicain Mike Rogers, et à Jocelyn Benson, candidate au poste de gouverneure. Obama était jusqu’à présent resté largement en retrait de la campagne démocrate sur le terrain. Mis à part une courte apparition en mai aux côtés du candidat au Sénat du Texas James Talarico – qui pourrait devenir le premier démocrate élu sénateur de l’État depuis 1988 – puis une vidéo de soutien, en juillet, à Josh Turek, candidat au Sénat en Iowa, il s’était surtout consacré à des levées de fonds et à l’enregistrement de spots de campagne. Des sondages favorables ou serrés dans des États remportés par Trump en 2024, au Texas mais aussi au Kansas et dans le Nebraska – où les démocrates soutiennent l’indépendant Dan Osborn –, pourraient priver les républicains de leur majorité à la chambre haute du Congrès. Avec une majorité à la Chambre des représentants pour laquelle les démocrates font figure de favoris, une telle victoire réduirait considérablement les marges d’action de Trump pour les deux dernières années de son mandat. Barack Obama est le plus populaire des anciens présidents encore en vie : selon un sondage CNN/SSRS conduit en mai, 57 % des Américains en ont une opinion favorable, contre 34 % pour Trump et 30 % pour Joe Biden CNN poll on presidents , CNN/SSRS, 18 juin 2026.'> 1 . Il est également le plus à même de jouer un rôle de « faiseur de rois » : selon une enquête NBC de septembre, 43 % des électeurs se disent plus enclins à voter pour un candidat soutenu par Obama, contre 33 % pour Bernie Sanders et 30 % pour Trump NBC September 2026 Poll , 20 septembre 2026.'> 2 . Son implication vise également à soutenir les finances des démocrates. Si les candidats du parti devancent leurs opposants républicains en levées de fonds dans plusieurs campagnes clefs (James Talarico au Texas, Adam Hamilton au Kansas, Troy Jackson dans le Maine…), les méga-donateurs républicains ont injecté des centaines de millions de dollars ces derniers mois dans les super-PAC qui soutiennent le GOP. À lui seul, Elon Musk a contribué environ 289 millions de dollars à des groupes républicains et à son propre super-PAC entre juillet et septembre. Le milliardaire, proche allié de Trump, a injecté 158 millions de dollars dans la course au Sénat au Texas pour soutenir le procureur général de l’État, Ken Paxton, qui affrontera Talarico le 3 novembre. Selon les derniers sondages, agrégés par l’analyste électoral Nate Silver, Talarico dispose d’une courte avance de 2,4 points. L’article À une semaine des élections de mi-mandat, Obama s’engage dans la campagne est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Mr Drew’s X Space outburst would not happen under my watch – NanaYaw Wiredu
items.description: Media entrepreneur and talent manager NanaYaw Wiredu says the recent social media incident involving Ghanaian musician Mr Drew would not have happened under his watch. Speaking on Woezor TV’s Breakfast Café , NanaYaw referred to Mr Drew’s heated exchange with a participant during an X Space discussion. The incident escalated after the participant addressed the singer as “chale”, prompting Mr Drew to insist that they were not age mates and to argue that differences in age and financial standing should command respect. The exchange ended with insults from both sides. “Recently you saw what happened to Mr Drew. It will never happen under my watch,” Nana Yaw said. He explained that artistes working with him are trained on how to speak on television, participate in radio interviews and respond when provoked. “Because you don’t want to put somebody off by saying the wrong thing,” he added. NanaYaw made the remarks during a discussion on building a successful music career. He stressed that artiste development involves more than producing hit songs and promoting music. It also requires preparing musicians to handle public attention and maintain a good relationship with their audience. Mr Drew’s X Space controversy The incident involving Mr Drew occurred during an X Space he hosted to interact with fans and promote his single Steeze . The discussion turned tense after a participant addressed him as “chale”, a popular Ghanaian expression often used informally among friends and peers. Mr Drew objected to the manner in which he was addressed, insisting that the participant was not his mate and arguing that differences in the age, social status and financial standing should be recognised. “I am not your mate. A lot of people think I am their mate, but I am not your mate. A lot of the boys think they are my age mates. When it comes to money and age, I am not your mate, and you need to put that in your head,” he said. The participant challenged the singer’s response, arguing that he was not an A-list artiste to make such a distinction. The exchange escalated, with both parties trading insults and Mr Drew threatening to block the participant. The confrontation attracted criticism on social media, with some users questioning the musician’s response, while others argued that artistes should be treated respectfully during online interactions. Mr Drew later clarified that his outburst was directed at trolls rather than his genuine fans. The importance of media training in artiste development NanaYaw Wiredu’s comments raises concerns about the importance of preparing musicians for public engagement as part of their professional development. Media training can help artistes communicate effectively during interviews, manage difficult questions and respond to provocation without escalating disagreements. In September 2023, Mr Wiredu, founder and creative director of Oneplay Africa, announced a free online Music Master Series aimed at helping emerging entertainment executives understand the business side of the music industry. His experience spans artiste management, publicity, publishing, events management and digital media. He has also managed artistes, including Nana Yaa, D-Flex and Mzbel, and worked on events such as Ghana Meets Naija and Mzbel at 10, according to published profiles. He is currently the PR Manager for Edem Goget’em.

items.title: Six-year-old’s death at Fofie Yam Festival: Family demands justice
items.description: The Akwamu Royal Family of Nchiraa in the Bono Region has appealed to the President, John Dramani Mahama, and the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to intervene in a fatal shooting incident that allegedly claimed the life of a six-year-old boy during the town’s Fofie Yam Festival. The deceased, Agyei Agyapong Gethro, was buried on Friday, October 23, 2026, following the incident on October 3, 2026. At a press conference, the acting head of the Akwamu Royal Family, Opanin Paul Kwabena Baffoe, called for a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The family also appealed to the Bono Regional Minister, the Wenchi Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and the Wenchi Divisional Police Command to intervene and provide answers to the bereaved family and the people of Nchiraa. It said it wanted the authorities to clarify what led to the shooting, identify those involved and explain the progress of police investigations. The family expressed concern about recurring misunderstandings and gunfire during celebrations of the Fofie Yam Festival, questioning why such incidents continued to occur during an occasion that should bring the community together. It called for calm while urging the security agencies to pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. The Assembly Member for the Dwomoo/Nteema Electoral Area, George Nketia, also appealed to the youth of Nchiraa to remain calm and allow the police to investigate the incident. He said those found to have been involved would be arrested, echoing the royal family’s call for accountability. Mr Nketia further cautioned the youth against carrying guns to public gatherings and other community events, warning against conduct that could lead to violence and loss of life.

items.title: Man held for torturing female scooty rider in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: The police on Friday claimed to have arrested a man who had allegedly tortured and injured a young woman riding a scooty on busy Mozang Link Road in the city. Identified as Ghulam Mustafa, the attacker was tracked down and arrested by the police with the help of data of dozens of the Punjab Safe Cities Authority (PSCA) cameras, besides using traditional investigation techniques. He was sent behind the bars after being nominated in a criminal case. A CCTV footage of the incident, which took place late on Thursday, sparked widespread public outrage once footage was aired. The footage showed the suspect overtook the scooty rider on the busy road, placed his bike in front of her two wheeler and subjected her to brutal torture in the presence of several passersby. It was shocking to observe that none of the onlookers tried to intervene and rescue the woman. The man pulled her hair and slapped her repeatedly. As per initial police reports, the woman suffered facial injuries, including nasal bone fracture, during the brutal attack. A police official says the attacker also threw the victim’s bag on the ground that contained a laptop valuing around Rs90,000, resulting in severe damage to the laptop. The suspect later fled the scene in the presence of several onlookers, he adds. A special police team, under the supervision of Civil Lines Superintendent of Police (SP) Maniza Karamat, tracked down and arrested the suspect using modern digital tracking technology. The official says that a case has been lodged against the attacker on the complaint of the victim’s father. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Une IA estime le risque de mortalité des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’un selfie
items.description: Des chercheurs américains ont développé un outil d’intelligence artificielle capable d’évaluer le risque de mortalité à court terme chez des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’une simple photographie du visage. Publiée dans la revue The Lancet Digital Health, cette étude ouvre des perspectives pour le suivi médical, tout en soulignant les limites de cette technologie. Une simple photo du visage pourrait-elle fournir des indications sur l’état de santé d’un patient atteint de cancer ? C’est la piste explorée par une équipe de chercheurs de l’hôpital Mass General Brigham, dans le Massachusetts, aux États-Unis. Leur outil, baptisé FAHR-FaceSurvival, utilise l’intelligence artificielle pour analyser certains traits du visage et estimer le risque de mortalité à court terme. Le modèle repose sur FAHR-Face, une intelligence artificielle préentraînée sur plus de 40 millions d’images faciales, puis adaptée à cette application médicale grâce à 34 363 photographies de patients atteints de cancer. Les chercheurs ont ensuite évalué ses performances sur un sous-groupe de 3 820 patients issu de la base de données Harvard-RT. Selon les résultats publiés dans The Lancet Digital Health, l’outil a identifié un groupe de 122 patients considérés comme présentant un risque élevé de mortalité. Parmi eux, 52,5 % sont décédés dans les 90 jours suivant l’évaluation. À l’inverse, seuls 2 % des 975 patients classés dans la catégorie de risque la plus faible sont décédés au cours de cette même période. Ces résultats suggèrent que les informations extraites d’une photographie faciale pourraient contribuer à repérer certains patients particulièrement vulnérables. Ils ne signifient toutefois pas qu’un selfie permet, à lui seul, de déterminer avec certitude l’évolution d’un cancer ou les chances de survie d’une personne. Une IA pour estimer aussi l’âge biologique Les chercheurs ont également développé un second outil, baptisé FAHR-FaceAge, conçu pour estimer l’âge biologique d’une personne à partir de son visage. Contrairement à l’âge chronologique, qui correspond au nombre d’années écoulées depuis la naissance, l’âge biologique cherche à refléter certains aspects du vieillissement de l’organisme. Testé sur plusieurs ensembles de données, ce modèle a notamment permis d’observer des différences de mortalité à court terme selon l’écart entre l’âge biologique estimé et l’âge réel des patients. Parmi 1 060 patients dont l’âge biologique estimé dépassait d’au moins 20 ans leur âge chronologique, 21 % sont décédés dans les 90 jours suivant l’évaluation. À l’opposé, environ 6 % des 4 195 patients dont l’âge biologique estimé était inférieur d’au moins dix ans à leur âge réel sont décédés pendant la même période. Les chercheurs soulignent que les deux outils apportent des informations complémentaires. Les résultats de FAHR-FaceAge et de FAHR-FaceSurvival sont faiblement corrélés, et leurs associations avec la survie restent indépendantes lorsqu’ils sont étudiés conjointement. L’étude relève également que certains facteurs liés au mode de vie, notamment le tabagisme et une consommation importante d’alcool, sont associés à un vieillissement prématuré du visage. Les modifications cosmétiques, comme le maquillage ou la chirurgie esthétique, n’ont pas affecté les performances de FAHR-FaceAge dans les tests rapportés. Des résultats prometteurs, mais des limites importantes Pour les auteurs, ces technologies pourraient, à terme, compléter les évaluations médicales classiques. Les photographies faciales présentent notamment l’avantage d’être faciles et peu coûteuses à obtenir, ce qui pourrait faciliter leur utilisation dans certains contextes de soins. Les chercheurs insistent néanmoins sur un point essentiel : ces outils ne sont pas destinés à remplacer les médecins ni à se substituer à leur jugement clinique. Ils pourraient plutôt contribuer à enrichir l’évaluation de l’état de santé et à accompagner certaines décisions thérapeutiques personnalisées. La performance de ces modèles devra donc être confirmée par des recherches supplémentaires, dans des contextes médicaux et auprès de populations plus diversifiés. The post Une IA estime le risque de mortalité des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’un selfie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: AIPAC’s shift
items.description: ON Wednesday, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) made an unusual announcement . The organisation would no longer endorse or make direct contributions to candidates running in US elections. This marks the end of a practice that AIPAC began in 2021 (its lobbying started in the ‘50s). This does not mean that the Israel lobby will stop trying to influence US elections. AIPAC will continue mobilising individual donors. However, the announcement is an acknowledgement of the growing difficulties associated with overt affiliation with the lobby and the pro-Israel agenda. The genocide in Gaza and the war in Iran have created a situation where many Americans are questioning their country’s support for Israel and the resources devoted to it. Democratic candidates have challenged US involvement in the Middle East and the $3.8 billion in annual assistance Washington provides Israel. No campaign has illustrated this with greater clarity than that of Dr Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the US Senate seat in Michigan. In the Democratic primary, AIPAC spent $30 million backing El-Sayed’s opponent, Haley Stevens. Other political action committees also spent heavily on her campaign. In contrast, El-Sayed spent only $3.2m, most of it raised from individual donors. Despite all this, El-Sayed won. One reason was his willingness to confront Stevens over AIPAC’s involvement in the race and to question why US taxpayer money should go to another country. What El-Sayed was able to do is connect two different realities of the American political context. First, he tapped into the American fatigue with interminable wars in the Middle East. Again, and again, he argued that the US had “no business” becoming embroiled in further conflicts, while infrastructure and institutions at home were decaying. His criticism of Donald Trump’s escapades in Iran became part of this argument. Second, El-Sayed connected the affordability crisis facing Americans to questions about government spending and the country’s relationship with Israel. Americans struggling to afford healthcare and basic groceries are naturally questioning how public money is spent abroad. War-weary Americans can see through Israeli machinations. El-Sayed is not campaigning on Israel alone. Affordability and healthcare are central issues for him, and he supports a government-funded Medicare For All option that would make healthcare accessible to millions of people. His own background in public health makes him a persuasive speaker on these issues. AIPAC’s affiliated Super PAC has now directed spending against El-Sayed in his contest with Republican Mike Rogers. This is a departure from AIPAC’s usual support for Democratic candidates in Michigan. American Zionists and the well-heeled donors behind AIPAC may see the Michigan contest not simply as an electoral battle in a US state but also as an indicator of how anti-Israel sentiment is becoming increasingly pervasive among the Democratic electorate. The announcement that there will be no more overt endorsements reflects the liability that public association with AIPAC can create for some candidates. It is a sea change in the character of Democratic politics in the US. There are global implications in this shift. If El-Sayed wins — and one hopes he does despite the millions that AIPAC is now pouring into his opponent’s coffers — it will mean that other Democratic lawmakers in the House and Senate will have to think twice about voting to send billions of dollars to Israel. In the past, Democratic politicians have voted en masse for just these sorts of measures. Israel is very proud of its genocidal actions in Gaza. It is also quite smug about having persua­d­­ed Trump to at­­tack Iran. It sees both of these act­ions and its continuing excesses in Gaza and the West Bank as victories. This, however, is an illusion. The reality is that in the process of achieving the former, Israelis forgot that ordinary, war-weary Americans can see through its machinations. This is important not because Israel cares what Americans think but because Israel is entirely dependent on the US, receiving almost 70 per cent of its military equipment from them. As the election of Zohran Mamdani in New York City and the hopeful rise of Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan show, Americans are signalling just how fed up they are with Israel’s intrusions in their own government and its attempts to create dual loyalties in their political leadership. As American leaders stop signing blank cheques for Israel as in the past five decades, Israel is likely to face enormous struggles. Already an isolated nation, increasingly detested by the world for the carnage of innocents, its future is not that of a victorious nation but of a widely reviled one. The writer is an attorney teaching constitutional law and political philosophy. rafia.zakaria@gmail.com Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Beyond tariff cuts
items.description: PAKISTAN cannot build a competitive industry by protecting it indefinitely. Nor can reducing protection, by itself, turn domestic manufacturers into exporters. Tariffs shape investment decisi­o­­ns, but competitiveness also depends on energy, te­­­chnology, scale, supply chains, market access, and security. A credible industrial strategy must address them together. Unconditional protection raises prices, blunts incentives to innovate, and rewards selling to a captive home market. Consu­mers finance inefficiency, and capital chases protected returns rather than export opportunities. Where there is no credible prospect of competitiveness, protection merely postpones adjustment at public expense. The National Tariff Policy 2025-30 , therefore, points broadly in the right direction. Fewer tariff slabs, cheaper imported inputs, and phased elimination of additional customs and regulatory duties can lower costs and reduce the bias against exports. But these are instruments of competitiveness, not substitutes for the conditions that make exports possible. The essential complement is a measurable programme to cut the costs the state imposes on production. If manufacturers face a timetable for lower protection, the government should face one for affordable, reliable energy, prompt tax refunds, simpler regulation, and efficient logistics. Otherwise, industry is asked to adjust while the state’s own contribution to uncompetitiveness goes unaddressed. This is not an argument for waiting until every domestic problem is solved; that would make protection permanent. It is a case for distinguishing activities with little prospect of competitiveness, those capable of achieving it, and a narrow set of strategic capabilities. The polyester chain shows the cost of failing to draw these distinctions. The textile industry association, APTMA, argues that protection on polyester staple fibre and its key input, purified terephthalic acid, raises costs for downstream textiles, while the country’s sole PTA plant, commissioned in 1998, lags newer plants in China and India. These claims by interested users warrant independent examination. The test is straightforward. Has prolonged support delivered globally competitive costs, technological upgrading, and lower energy use per tonne? Has it helped downstream producers compete in synthetic and blended textiles? Protection that preserves an inefficient input supplier while handicapping a much larger export opportunity defeats its own purpose. Energy illustrates the shared responsibility. High electricity tariffs and excessive electricity consumption are different problems: the government must fix the first; manufacturers must invest to reduce the second. Consumers and downstream exporters should not indefinitely finance either failure. Protection that preserves an inefficient input supplier while handicapping a much larger export opportunity defeats its own purpose. Yet an equally indiscriminate withdrawal of support could destroy capabilities with a viable future. Auto parts deserve assessment on this basis. Complaints about expensive vehicles and meagre exports obscure engineering skills within the supplier base. Toolmaking, casting, machining, moulding, process control, and quality assurance are not tied to one vehicle. Partnerships with foreign manufacturers can develop capabilities serving replacement markets, other engineering industries, and, where specifications permit, defence production. These capabilities justify scrutiny and selective development, not permanent protection for every assembler or component. The right unit of assessment is often the product or process, not the entire sector. Scale is crucial. Investment in moulds, testing or automated lines must be recovered over sufficient output; short runs make each unit expensive. Too many models fragment demand in a small market, while differing specifications prevent vendors from supplying the same part to several assemblers. Policy should encourage viable specialisation, common components where feasible, supplier consolidation, and access to replacement and export markets. A vendor serving several customers can reach volumes that no single low-volume model offers. Competition policy must accompany consolidation, so that scale raises productivity rather than market power. Upstream supply matters too. Reliable access to automotive-grade steel, engineering plastics and specialised chemicals affects quality, cost, lead times, and working capital. A competitive local supplier can shorten delivery and support joint development, but domestic steel or petrochemical production alone guarantees neither. Pakistan need not make every input before it can export. Where domestic production lacks scale or technology, predictable access to competitively priced imports is essential; forcing manufacturers to buy costly local inputs shifts protection upstream and erodes downstream competitiveness. The goal is an efficient supply chain combining viable domestic capabilities with dependable imports, not local-content targets. Market access is the next missing piece. Cutting Pakistan’s import tariffs does nothing to lower the duties its exporters face abroad. Preferential trade agreements can open larger markets, but their value depends on product coverage, rules of origin, and real commercial opportunities. They should be negotiated around what Pakistan can competitively supply and what investors could realistically produce. Buyers also weigh security. Export relationships depend on plant visits, technical assistance, audits, and dependable delivery. Insecurity, transport disruptions or barriers to foreign experts can cancel out a competitive price. Buyers pay for reliability, and investors need confidence that people, equipment and goods can travel safely. How, then, should protection be withdrawn? Activities with no credible route to competitiveness should have a clear exit timetable. Those with demonstrable potential should receive temporary support tied to investment, productivity, quality, energy efficiency, and a narrowing price gap with imports. Government should accept published obligations on costs and business conditions. An independent review should distinguish policy failures from outdated equipment, inadequate scale, or poor management. Verified government failures could justify limited adjustments to the tariff timetable, each with a firm expiry. Industry must not gain a permanent veto over reform. Strategic exceptions should remain narrow. Food security can justify agricultural resilience without self-sufficiency in every crop. Defence can justify selected domestic capabilities despite higher costs, subject to periodic review of their security value and expense. Lower tariffs on inputs remove one obstacle to exports. They cannot supply scale, modern technology, efficiency, market access, or security. Pakistan needs a reciprocal bargain: industry must earn support through performance, and the government must deliver conditions for competition. Neither should hand consumers an indefinite bill for its failures. The writeris a former CEO of Unilever Pakistan and of the Pakistan Business Council. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

Burkina : le gouvernement veut mobiliser 67,2 milliards pour renforcer l’autonomie économique des ménages vulnérables en 5 ans
items.description: Le Conseil des ministres a marqué jeudi son accord pour la ratification d’un financement de 67,2 milliards de FCFA destiné à la mise en œuvre du Projet d’autonomisation économique des ménages pauvres et vulnérables pour la résilience et la protection sociale adaptative (PARPS), qui vise à soutenir 120 000 ménages pauvres et vulnérables sur l’ensemble du territoire national sur une période de cinq ans. Selon le compte rendu du Conseil des ministres, le projet prévoit notamment l’organisation de 120 000 ménages pauvres et vulnérables en coopératives communautaires autour d’unités économiques, ainsi que la mise en place de 4 800 coopératives communautaires et de 1 200 unités économiques locales destinées à soutenir les activités de production et de transformation. Il prévoit également la construction de six magasins d’une capacité de 5 000 tonnes chacun, de deux entrepôts modernes de stockage et de 20 magasins d’une capacité de 1 000 tonnes chacun. En matière de logistique, le projet prévoit l’acquisition de huit véhicules, de 20 camions monoblocs, de 20 camions-bennes et de deux camions-citernes. Sa mise en œuvre concernera prioritairement les régions des Koulsé, de Yaadga, du Nakambé, de Nando, des Bankui et du Sourou, en tenant compte du déploiement progressif du Registre social unique (RSU). La ratification de l’ordonnance relative à ce financement intervient conformément à la loi n°23-2025/ALT du 29 décembre 2025 portant habilitation du Gouvernement à autoriser, par voie d’ordonnance, la ratification des accords et conventions de financement signés entre le Burkina Faso et ses partenaires techniques et financiers. D’un montant total de 120 millions de dollars, soit 67 222 473 360 FCFA, ce financement est composé d’un accord de crédit et d’un accord de don signés le 14 juillet 2026 entre le Burkina Faso et l’Association internationale de développement (IDA), selon le compte rendu du Conseil des ministres du jeudi 22 octobre 2026. Agence d’information du Burkina NAK/yos/ata L’article Burkina : le gouvernement veut mobiliser 67,2 milliards pour renforcer l’autonomie économique des ménages vulnérables en 5 ans est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: ¿Dónde viven los caseros? Barrios de renta alta y zonas turísticas concentran a quienes declaran ingresos de alquiler
items.description: Los barrios de mayor renta del país y los distritos con mayor dinamismo turístico suelen concentrar una mayor proporción de contribuyentes que declaran en su IRPF ingresos por el alquiler de inmuebles . En algunas de las urbanizaciones más acomodadas y exclusivas del país, aproximadamente una de cada tres personas perciben rendimientos inmobiliarios. Dos ejemplos llamativos de Madrid son Fuente del Fresno (San Sebastián de los Reyes) y La Moraleja (Alcobendas), donde los porcentajes de caseros alcanzan el 39% y el 36%. La proporción también supera con holgura el 30% en otros barrios acomodados como Pla del Remei (Valencia), Ciudalcampo (San Sebastián de los Reyes) o Pedralbes-Sarriá y Vallvidrera-Tibidabo i Les Planes (Barcelona), en los que la renta media total por contribuyente supera los 100.000 euros. items.title: Breaking the cycle
items.description: THE World Bank’s latest Pakistan Development Update sets out what faster reforms could deliver for the economy. If policies and institutions matched those of an average middle-income country, it estimates, annual growth could reach 6.2-6.9pc , enough to reach Vietnam’s current income level, and incomes would triple by 2050. The distance from here is long. Real GDP growth rose to 3.65pc in FY26 and the primary surplus reached 2.9pc of GDP. But per capita income is currently growing at only about 1.6pc, which means the economy has been put in better financial order without making most people better off. The country’s return to macroeconomic stability is widely appreciated by international lenders and credit agencies. However, it is not the same thing as a solid foundation for rapid growth. Much of this stability has come from holding the economy down. High interest rates, fiscal tightening, and costly energy have dampened demand and squeezed imports, easing pressure on the external account. Workers’ remittances have helped the current account and rebuilt reserves, and continued external borrowing has bought time. But none of this builds capacity. Borrowing defers the bill, remittances bring in dollars without adding to domestic output, and compressed imports can fix the external balance while leaving exports no more competitive. The stability that results depends on inflows continuing and on the government keeping up its restraint. That is why any real push for growth can be risky. It would mean more imported machinery, fuel, industrial inputs, and consumer goods. If exports and productivity do not keep pace, the current account slips, reserves fall, and policymakers enforce tightening again. We have been through this cycle many times. Breaking it means changing what the economy produces and sells, not just how fast it is allowed to grow. The obstacles are well known: unreliable and costly energy, a narrow tax base, cumbersome regulation, weak competition, and a poorly skilled workforce. Policy keeps changing, which deters long-term investment. Tax reform must bring undertaxed sectors into the net, instead of increasing the burden on those already compliant. Energy reform has to cut system costs rather than shift them between consumers and the budget. And exports need a policy that works beyond incentives. Macroeconomic stability cannot carry the economy much further without better productivity. The World Bank’s numbers are best read as a reform target. Reaching Vietnam’s income level will take sustained spending on education, health, infrastructure, and technology, and institutions that can be trusted. It will also take growth that creates more than just better headline figures. If the government does not use the present breathing space to raise productivity, boost exports, and complete lasting energy and tax reforms, the next growth push could bring back the crisis Pakistan has just come out of. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Bolt Food’s Kumasi business has more than doubled as growth continues into its second year
items.description: Nearly two years after expanding to Kumasi, Bolt Food saw strong growth in the city, with activity increasing by more than 100% year-on-year in its second year of operations. The continued growth points to sustained adoption of app-based delivery beyond Accra and the growing role of Kumasi as an important market for Bolt Food in Ghana. Since entering Kumasi, Bolt Food has continued to connect customers with local restaurants through its platform, giving local restaurants and other food merchants an additional channel to reach customers beyond physical footfall. Bolt Food’s General Manager, Ali Zaryab, said Kumasi’s performance demonstrates why expanding beyond the capital was an important part of Bolt Food’s growth strategy in Ghana. “When we expanded Bolt Food to Kumasi, we saw an opportunity to serve one of Ghana’s largest and most commercially active cities. Nearly two years later, the fact that the business is still growing at more than 100% year-on-year shows that the demand was not simply an initial launch effect. Customers are continuing to adopt delivery as part of how they access restaurants and increasingly other everyday products across the city,” he said. The growth also reflects a broader evolution in how customers are using delivery platforms. While restaurant meals remain an important part of the delivery experience, the sustained growth suggests that delivery is becoming a familiar option for customers seeking convenience. “What is particularly encouraging about Kumasi is not just the growth, but the breadth of demand we’re beginning to see,” Zaryab added. “Food delivery may have been the starting point, but customers are increasingly looking for convenience across different parts of their day. That creates an opportunity for restaurants to reach customers in new ways.” Bolt Food said it will continue working with local merchants and couriers as it strengthens its operations in Kumasi and responds to changing customer demand. The performance comes as Bolt Food continues to grow its delivery offering in Ghana, connecting customers with restaurants and retailers through its app.

items.title: Viven fuera de Israel; ahora vuelven para votar contra Netanyahu
items.description: Shira Carmel se mueve por Israel con la extrañeza de quien lleva tres años sin pisar su país. Se mudó a Australia el 17 de octubre de 2023 y solo ha regresado ahora, para unas semanas. Lo ha hecho porque echar este martes en las urnas a Benjamín Netanyahu le importa más que todas las horas de viaje y que los 5.800 euros (6.500 dólares estadounidenses) que le han costado los cuatro billetes de avión de la familia. Israel es una de las escasas democracias que —salvo contadas excepciones— no permite votar, ni en Embajadas, ni por correo, a sus 810.000 mayores de edad en el extranjero. Por eso, se calcula que decenas de miles vuelan estos días para depositar físicamente la papeleta en unas elecciones consideradas cruciales , con la coalición del primer ministro y los partidos judíos de oposición casi empatados en los sondeos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El asedio ruso complica sobrevivir en Kramatorsk: “Cuando te quedas herido, es mejor que te maten”
items.description: “Tenemos suerte”, suspira Volodímir, de 77 años, asomado al balcón de su casa medio destruida en Kramatorsk. Delante, los hierros retorcidos y roídos por las llamas de lo que hasta una semana antes eran dos de los autobuses de línea de la ciudad. Una bomba planeadora rusa cayó en medio de ambos y mató a 30 personas el 8 de octubre . Volodímir y su mujer, Ludmila, de 67 años, habían salido unos minutos antes al mercado. Al regresar, se toparon sin esperarlo con el infierno en la calle Yuvileina, que transcurre delante de su edificio. “Tenemos suerte”, repite incidiendo en los cuantiosos daños que sufre su apartamento al tiempo que acaba de cubrir las ventanas con tablones facilitados por unos soldados. items.title: Edo govt, NLC strike peace deal as Labour moves to restore electricity
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Edo State Government have resolved their prolonged dispute, with the state government agreeing to recognise the NLC caretaker committee. As part of the truce, the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, is expected to take steps towards restoring electricity to the state that has been in total darkness since Monday. The NLC Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, said the resolution followed a meeting brokered by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, at his residence on Friday, October 23, 2026. According to Upah, the meeting was attended by the Edo State Governor, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, former Governor of the State and Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole and the Minister of Labour and Employment. Upah said, “The long-running dispute between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Edo State Government on the non-recognition of the NLC caretaker committee in Edo State has been brought to an end. “At a meeting brokered by the SGF at his residence today, Friday, October 23, 2026, between the Edo State Government, represented by the governor, and the NLC, represented by President Comrade Joe Ajaero, the governor accepted to recognise and work with the NLC caretaker committee in Edo State as the lawful representative of the NLC. “The governor also agreed to ensure that check-off dues are remitted through the appropriate channels to the NLC.” On the steps to consolidate the peace agreement, Upah said the Edo State governor had requested a meeting with the caretaker committee. “As part of the peace initiative, the Edo State governor requested the Congress president to lead the caretaker committee to pay him a courtesy visit in Benin City,” he said. Upah further disclosed that the NLC secretariat in Edo State, which had remained under lock and key amid the dispute, would reopen immediately. “The Congress Secretariat in Edo State, which has been under lock and key by some people who presented themselves as acting for and on behalf of the governor, even as the governor denied knowledge or acquiescence of their actions, is to reopen immediately,” he said. He added that the agreement would restore normal relations between the state government and organised labour. “The regular or normal statutory relationship between the state government and the NLC is to resume with immediate effect,” Upah stated. On electricity supply, the NLC Acting General Secretary said the labour movement had also undertaken to facilitate the restoration of power to the state. “On the NLC’s part, NUEE is to restore power to Edo State as soon as practicable,” he said. Upah recalled that the dispute had escalated over what the Congress described as anti-labour actions by the Edo State Government. “It will be recalled that the prolonged anti-labour actions of the government, which constituted interference, intimidation and bullying, compelled the NLC to lodge a complaint against the Edo State Government at the International Labour Organisation (ILO), for which Nigeria was indicted,” he said. The agreement is expected to pave the way for the reopening of the NLC secretariat, the resumption of normal industrial relations, the proper remittance of check-off dues and steps towards restoring electricity in Edo State. Observers believe the full implementation of the resolutions will be crucial to sustaining the peace agreement and preventing a recurrence of the dispute between the state government and organised labour. items.title: ¿Dónde y por qué se protesta en Europa? Las reivindicaciones de los jóvenes de cada país
items.description: Media Europa vuelve a salir a la calle este sábado. Hay convocatorias desde Grecia hasta Bélgica, pasando por Albania, Francia, Portugal y España. Son las últimas de un otoño de movilizaciones : entre el 15 de septiembre y el 23 de octubre, 12 países europeos suman al menos 177 protestas o manifestaciones. La cifra es parecida a la media de 190 protestas mensuales entre septiembre y octubre de los otoños más intensos de la crisis del euro (2010, 2011 y 2012), según los registros de PolDem, un proyecto universitario que recopila protestas a partir de noticias de agencias. Francia, España, Italia, Portugal y Bélgica concentran la mayoría de las movilizaciones contabilizadas. items.title: Cinco días frenéticos en los consulados para cumplir el ultimátum del Supremo: “Es como reparar un avión en pleno vuelo”
items.description: “Nos va a volver locos este asunto”. Una fuente consular resume así el desconcierto que se ha instalado estos días en los consulados, obligados a hacer frente a una carrera contrarreloj para cumplir con la orden del Tribunal Supremo de identificar a los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos que hayan acreditado la condición de exiliados de sus antepasados. Este viernes, el alto tribunal puso en marcha la cuenta atrás, y dio cinco días a los ministerios de Exteriores y Justicia para que remitan a la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, a la Junta Electoral Central y a la Oficina del Censo Electoral los nombres de los 163.020 afectados por la suspensión del derecho al voto . items.title: Leer a Pedro Almodóvar: “El escritor es egoísta por naturaleza”
items.description: Libros que los personajes escriben, leen, regalan. Libros que saltan de una película a otra, que inspiran tramas, que se adaptan. La filmografía de Pedro Almodóvar está plagada de referencias literarias. Ha publicado numerosos relatos a lo largo de las décadas, algunos de ellos reunidos en El último sueño (2023). Pero ha esperado hasta los 77 años para publicar su primera novela: El hombre que solo escribía en los aviones (Reservoir Books), que llega a las librerías el 29 de octubre. Un libro frenético y libre, como su cine, atravesado por la pasión lectora. Lo protagoniza Flavio Guijarro, nueva incorporación al fecundo plantel de personajes almodovarianos. Un coach de autores obsesionado con escribir. Como tantos protagonistas del manchego, Flavio tiene mucho de él. Es sabido que la obra de Almodóvar es un ente poroso por el que circulan la ficción, la realidad, lo vivido, lo escuchado, lo leído. Esta entrevista discurre por esos poros y se centra en el Almodóvar lector y escritor. Recibe a Babelia en las oficinas madrileñas de El Deseo, su productora, con las paredes llenas de recuerdos y carteles de sus películas llegados de todos los rincones del mundo. Preside su despacho una gran estantería llena de libros que, advierte, son sobre todo novedades que le llegan. Su biblioteca más personal, admite, está en su casa. Sobre la mesa, eso sí, el último libro que le ha fascinado, Cosamala, de Alana S. Portero , autora hacia la que se deshace en elogios. Se enciende la grabadora y aparece un Almodóvar sereno, amable, cómodo con una conversación ajena a la clásica promoción del cine, alejado de la ansiedad que, dice, ha sido un motor de su novela. Seguir leyendo El hombre que solo escribía en los aviones Pedro Almodóvar Reservoir Books, 2026 256 páginas. 20,90 euros A la venta el 29 de octubre

items.title: Neurodivergentes: la etiqueta de moda para los cerebros fuera de lo común
items.description: A Paloma le dijeron que su hija, con altas capacidades, era neurodivergente. Poco después le sugirieron que su hijo, con hipersensibilidad emocional, quizá entrara también en esa categoría, que a Paloma le sonó sugestiva y misteriosa, con un toque exclusivo, como de mente fuera del rebaño. En ambos casos se lo comunicaron en el colegio donde lleva a sus retoños, durante sendas reuniones con el equipo de psicopedagogía. Paloma se lo comentó entonces a su psicóloga, quien aportó una nueva evaluación: con dos niños así, lo más probable era que la madre fuese, asimismo, neurodivergente. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La fiscalía de Cataluña niega a tres víctimas el acceso a la investigación sobre las violaciones que sufrieron
items.description: Los dos violadores eran siempre los mismos y la violencia y el modus operandi empleados, idénticos. Juntos cometieron dos olas de violaciones durante los años noventa en Cataluña, pero solo uno de ellos fue detenido y condenado, y nunca delató a su cómplice. Hace un año, tres víctimas de aquellas agresiones —hubo al menos 16, cuatro de ellas menores de edad— pidieron a la Fiscalía de esa comunidad que ampliara los análisis de ADN para tratar de identificar al cómplice . La fiscalía abrió unas diligencias preprocesales de investigación. Los análisis se ampliaron y se obtuvo el perfil genético del segundo autor, pero dado que los delitos han prescrito, el fiscal superior, Francisco Bañeres, archivó las diligencias el 27 de julio pasado. Y aunque en el decreto de archivo reconocía expresamente “el legítimo interés” de las tres mujeres en saber la verdad, en la práctica no se ha atendido. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cataluña plantea prohibir los parques infantiles con caucho reciclado por salud
items.description: En los últimos días hemos leído noticias sobre los riesgos de los parques infantiles de caucho reciclado. ¿Cómo de peligrosos pueden ser para los niños? No hay que alarmarse, pero la evidencia científica muestra que estos entornos contienen sustancias que actúan como disruptores endocrinos , cuya acumulación altera el equilibrio hormonal; aunque por ahora cumplen los límites legales, el principio de prudencia aconseja sustituirlos por otros de tierra o vegetación. Cataluña ya plantea prohibir las zonas infantiles elaboradas con este material, algo que ha incluido en su anteproyecto de ley de residuos, pero ni el Gobierno central, ni las comunidades, ni los ayuntamientos ni la Comisión Europea proponen hacer lo mismo. El sector recuerda que este reciclaje cumple la ley, mientras los expertos critican que la normativa actual es muy laxa y recuerdan lo que pasó con el bisfenol A , cuya cantidad segura se redujo en 20.000 veces. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La vida precaria de los bomberos de Ávila: alguien se olvidó de contratar la luz en la nueva estación
items.description: Los bomberos de Ávila miran por el cristal. Detrás del vidrio hay una cocina, un frigorífico, sillas y mesas. Todo nuevecito, envuelto en plástico, en un módulo prefabricado junto a unas duchas y vestuarios. Todo está listo dentro de la nueva estación, pero no pueden usar nada de eso. Así ha sido desde hace un año, porque la Junta de Castilla y León (PP y Vox) pagó la infraestructura, pero no los contratos de la luz ni del agua. “¡Es increíble!”, exclaman los brigadistas que coinciden en que es “un garaje de 420.000 euros”. Tampoco hay un hidrante donde cargar los vehículos y tiran de los de El Tiemblo, donde se encuentran perdiendo el tiempo. Estos ejemplos ilustran las quejas del gremio, que se siente desatendido y mal dirigido después de vivir el peor verano de su historia . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los murales para el Waldorf Astoria de Nueva York en 1929 acaban en Boadilla tras una disputa entre Madrid y Cataluña
items.description: Se crearon para decorar el hotel más exclusivo de Nueva York y han terminado protegidas por Madrid en la ciudad financiera del Banco Santander en Boadilla del Monte. Para cubrir ese viaje transoceánico de casi un siglo, las quince pinturas murales de Josep María Sert , pintor de vida novelesca, y testigo de las convulsiones de un tiempo marcado por la Guerra Civil y las dos guerras mundiales, han protagonizado un recorrido excepcional. Primero, por su coste: 150.000 dólares de 1929, una cifra nunca vista, “desorbitada”, en descripción de los técnicos de la Comunidad de Madrid que las han estudiado. Luego, por su emplazamiento original: el hotel Waldorf Astoria , por entonces la medida del lujo, que honró al artista bautizando una sala con su nombre (la Sert Room) sin esperar a que muriera, como destacó él mismo. Y finalmente, por haber estado en un limbo administrativo inusitado: aunque la Generalitat de Cataluña fue quien inició los trámites para declarar Bien de Interés Cultural los lienzos cuando volvieron a España (lo que impide venderlos en el extranjero y obliga a conservarlos) ha sido Madrid quien ha logrado darles esa protección casi 40 años después. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Ayuntamiento planea pasar los gastos de limpieza y desperfectos a los acampados de Sol: “Que no cueste un euro a los madrileños”
items.description: Ni un euro. El Ayuntamiento de Madrid quiere pasar los gastos que deriven de la acampada de la Puerta del Sol ―limpieza, reparaciones, desperfectos― a quienes están durmiendo o han dormido en el campamento. Con estas palabras lo expuso la vicealcaldesa, Inma Sanz: “Por supuesto, trataremos de repercutir hasta el último euro que se vaya a gastar este Ayuntamiento a los causantes de esta situación, que son los que están allí de manera ilegal y los que lo están consintiendo por dejación de funciones [por la delegación del Gobierno]. No vamos a parar hasta tratar de que a los madrileños no nos cueste un euro”, dijo el jueves en la rueda de prensa semanal posterior a la Junta de Gobierno, sin explicar nada más al respecto. A cómo prevén hacerlo, un portavoz responde que “se está estudiando”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Rompedora, sexualizada, legendaria: Lara Croft y ‘Tomb Raider’ cumplen 30 años de aventuras
items.description: Tal vez celebre con su plato favorito: una tosta de alubias cocidas. O quizás se conceda alguna galleta de chocolate con naranja, el otro manjar que adora. Lo cierto es que este sábado Lara Croft se merece al menos una pequeña pausa entre tantas aventuras. Está acostumbrada a sumar hitos, pero hoy festeja uno especial: 30 años desde el lanzamiento del primer Tomb Raider. Tan apasionada de historia, la arqueóloga lleva tres décadas escribiendo la del videojuego , junto con la suya. Y, probablemente, de la cultura popular, a juzgar por los 100 millones de copias vendidas, las 2.300 portadas de revistas, las exposiciones, películas o canciones que ha protagonizado. “Te asombraría lo persuasiva que puedo ser, incluso con hombres peligrosos”, afirmaba en uno de sus juegos. Sobran los hechos para darle la razón. Ni siquiera hace falta que saque sus célebres dos pistolas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La mujer que cosió un supermercado: “Me dedico a crear universos paralelos hechos de fieltro”
items.description: Lucy Sparrow (Bath, Reino Unido, 40 años) es una de las creadoras más disruptivas del mundo. Sus trabajos, siempre situados en entornos cotidianos y comunitarios para “resultar inmediatamente reconocibles para cualquier público” han ido creciendo en ambición, volumen y expansión desde su primera instalación, en 2014, llamada Corner Shop. “Erra una tienda tradicional británica de barrio que llené con 4.000 objetos hechos a mano con fieltro. Tras el éxito de aquella exposición, asumí el reto de llevar mi práctica artística hacia exposiciones cada vez más grandes y complejas, hasta llegar a la instalación de 1.000 metros cuadrados que actualmente se puede visitar en The Momentary Museum de Bentonville, Arkansas”, cuenta Sparrow a ICON. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Matar a un oso’: la serie que cuenta cómo el asesinato de un plantígrado se convirtió en una exhaustiva investigación judicial
items.description: Fue una de las muertes más sonadas ocurridas durante el confinamiento de 2020. Y eso que el asesinado era un oso, Cachou, plantígrado poco querido por los ganaderos del Valle de Arán porque en los meses anteriores a su muerte se había cebado con la ganadería equina. Pero el crimen escondía conflictos lastrados, enfrentamientos soterrados y dio pie a una investigación judicial con secreto de sumario incluido, un cóctel que ha acabado convertido en serie, Matar a un oso, liderada por los hermanos Sánchez-Cabezudo, y que Movistar Plus estrena el 10 de diciembre, aunque antes se ha proyectado, este viernes, en la primera jornada de la Seminci. Ha llegado antes un producto audiovisual que una sentencia: los dos acusados por el asesinato del plantígrado aún siguen a la espera de juicio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Juicio latino al trumpismo
items.description: Estados Unidos ya lleva una semana votando y los primeros datos del sufragio anticipado para las legislativas del 3 de noviembre transmiten que los estadounidenses tienen ganas de decir algo en las urnas sobre la situación de su país. Aún no sabemos exactamente qué es. Hasta el viernes, ya habían participado más de 23 millones de personas, un aumento generalizado respecto a 2022. En Texas, donde está en juego un escaño del Senado que supondría un vuelco político sensacional si cayera en manos demócratas, las dos principales áreas metropolitanas, Dallas y Houston, registraron un récord de votos en el primer día hábil, el pasado lunes. El 30% de los electores de Texas son latinos. Las encuestas generales indican más movilización entre los demócratas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Perder las formas
items.description: Manuel Fernández-Montesinos apenas se acordaba de su padre ni de su tío Federico, asesinados los dos, con un día de diferencia, cuando él tenía cuatro años. Las fotos le concedían un espejismo de memoria. En la vida de un niño las personas desaparecen y nadie se ocupa de darle explicaciones, por un deseo de protección que a Fernández-Montesinos le pareció siempre equivocado. El padre y el tío tan querido unas veces están y otras ya no están, y ni siquiera vuelven a aparecer en ese porvenir indeterminado de la conciencia infantil, regresados de un viaje, trayendo ese regalo que quizás el niño no olvide nunca, aunque no pueda recordar al que fue su porrtador. El espacio en blanco de los muertos lo ocuparon en la niñez y la juventud de Manuel Fernández-Montesinos dos hombres mayores que a él se lo parecerían más aún, físicamente bien sólidos, a diferencia de los queridos fantasmas fotográficos, con un aspecto formal de señores de otro tiempo, casi de otro siglo: su abuelo Federico y quien él llamó siempre el tío Fernando, Fernando de los Ríos. En las fotos don Federico García Rodríguez tiene una gran cabeza cuadrada sobre un torso cuadrado y fornido, más rotundo aún por los hombros rectos y las anchas solapas de la chaqueta de un traje negro que durante los últimos nueve años de su vida fue un traje invariable de luto. En el paraíso de la Huerta de San Vicente , en la que el niño conoció y perdió muy pronto la eternidad feliz del verano, el abuelo era el gigante bondadoso que velaba por el nieto y le regalaba caramelillos y herramientas de hortelano hechas a la medida de las manos y las fuerzas infantiles por un herrero amigo. La silueta de encina del abuelo se recorta con la misma nitidez en la huerta familiar, en la cubierta del barco donde lo que queda de la familia va a exiliarse en Estados Unidos, en la orilla del río Hudson y entre los robles y los arces de Riverside Park, donde el antiguo niño hortelano ahora juega al beisbol y habla inglés sin ningún rastro de acento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Susan Sarandon: “A veces me llaman comunista. Creo que es la manera que tienen algunos de decir que alguien está como una cabra”
items.description: El 25 de septiembre, apenas una semana después de esta entrevista, Susan Sarandon (Nueva York, 80 años) fue detenida a las puertas de la ONU en Nueva York. Protestaba, junto a otras actrices como Hannah Einbinder o Cynthia Nixon , contra la comparecencia en la Asamblea del primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu. No era la primera vez que la detenían y quizás no sea la última. Susan Sarandon, actriz en más de 100 películas, ha protagonizado éxitos de Hollywood como El cliente, Quédate a mi lado o Las brujas de Eastwick; películas de culto como The Rocky Horror Picture Show o Thelma y Louise ; y películas comprometidas como Pena de muerte , que le valió un Oscar. Ha aparecido en la serie Friends y ha rodado con Louis Malle. Porque Sarandon escoge sus proyectos como vive, de forma desprejuiciada, con una mezcla de curiosidad y desafío: “Cuando leo un guion quiero que me conmueva. Quiero que el personaje sea algo que no haya hecho antes. Está muy bien si hay un director con una buena trayectoria, pero a veces son directores nuevos. Es genial si te pueden pagar, pero a veces no pueden”. Es el caso de su último proyecto, The Accompanist (aún pendiente de título en español), donde interpreta a Sylvia, una madre de acogida atormentada y excéntrica. items.title: Cooperativas para comprar vivienda a precio de coste: ¿una fórmula olvidada para aliviar la crisis de acceso?
items.description: Solo 18 días después del final de la Guerra Civil, el 19 de abril de 1939, se creó el Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda para hacer frente a la grave escasez de casas y a la destrucción del parque residencial provocada por el conflicto. Entre las fórmulas utilizadas figuraba las cooperativas, que han permitido la construcción de más de 2,5 millones de viviendas desde 1957, alrededor del 10% del parque residencial español, según la Confederación de Cooperativas de Viviendas y Rehabilitación de España (Concovi). items.title: Wendy Brown, politóloga: “Llevamos un tipo de vida insostenible y lo sabemos”
items.description: En esta época posterior a todo y anterior a nada, la politóloga Wendy Brown va a lo fundamental. Habla de la transcendencia de las próximas elecciones , de la espiral nihilista del neoliberalismo, del problemón de la lógica masculinista naturalizada, de las demandas que comparten los votantes de izquierda y derecha, y de los movimientos sociales que buscan salida a un mundo en combustión, víctima de un fuego alimentado por demagogos oportunistas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Es real ese pelo en la sopa? La IA llega a las reclamaciones en restaurantes
items.description: Este verano, un restaurante gallego denunciaba que unos clientes intentaron no pagar la cuenta apoyándose en un vídeo en el que aparecían insectos sobre el mantel. El local sospechó que las imágenes estaban manipuladas con inteligencia artificial , amenazó con llamar a la policía y los comensales acabaron pagando. El caso se hizo viral cuando Jesús Soriano, creador de la cuenta Soy Camarero , difundió lo sucedido en redes sociales tras recibirlo directamente del establecimiento. “Me llegó por Instagram, por mensaje privado, y estuve hablando con los dueños porque era la primera vez que veía algo así”, explica. No cree que vaya a ser la última: “Cuanto más avance esta tecnología, seguro que comienzan a llover los casos”. La picaresca española lleva perfeccionándose desde el siglo XVI, y del Lazarillo de Tormes al simpa con IA han cambiado las herramientas, pero no tanto el impulso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Palos de ciego’, una columna por dentro
items.description: El título genérico de la columna, ‘Palos de ciego’, se me apareció mientras daba vueltas a una frase de William Faulkner : “La literatura tiene el mismo impacto que una cerilla encendida en medio de un campo en medio de la noche; la cerilla ilumina relativamente poco, pero nos permite ver cuánta oscuridad nos rodea”. Esta columna siempre ha aspirado a entregarle al lector un pedazo de prosa decente, a entretenerle un rato, a hacerle un poco de compañía; en el mejor de los casos, a que ambos, lector y autor, podamos intuir a tientas algo de la oscuridad que nos rodea. No se me ocurre un propósito más ambicioso. Seguir leyendo El País Semanal 50 Aniversario Este artículo forma parte del especial aniversario de la revista que se publica en su edición impresa el domingo 25 de octubre.

items.title: Manual de supervivencia para el periodo electoral
items.description: Antes de disfrutar de la juerga electoral recuerde que detrás de cada adversario hay un ser humano que ha sufrido lo mismo que usted. Y por lo mismo que usted. Y sepa que si aún no lo ha hecho, lo hará. Es importante por eso que se abstenga de llamar a sus rivales políticos como si fueran tribus en vez de personas . No diga zurdo, no diga facha, no diga fascista en estos días. Su lenguaje no modificará los votos y empobrecerá el diálogo. Un adversario agresivo no es más que un adversario que tiene miedo. Si usted es agresivo con él, tendrá aún más miedo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dafne Fernández, actriz: “Nunca me ha gustado escuchar cosas positivas de mí, quizás porque siempre me han dicho las negativas”
items.description: Dafne Fernández (Madrid, 41 años) acapara las miradas desde un rincón. La actriz y bailarina ha entrado sigilosa en el Salón Carlos III del Teatro Real de Madrid , donde una veintena de periodistas e influencers esperan a que imparta un breve taller de danza clásica con motivo del 25º aniversario de la película Barbie en El Cascanueces (2001), del que es la embajadora en España. Ya en el centro de la sala, después de agradecer su nombramiento y de dar las primeras indicaciones, parece tan cercana que apetece seguirla. Plié, demi-plié, relevé; las presentes intentan imitar sus movimientos hasta que, de pronto, rompe la disciplina y se sienta en el suelo, animando al resto a hacer lo mismo mientras suena el emocionante Pas de Deux compuesto por Chaikovski para el ballet estrenado en 1892: “Así supe lo que era el síndrome de Stendhal. Es la música que me pongo cuando paso por un momento difícil y quiero escapar a otro lugar”, dice. Mientras, en el suelo, escucha con los ojos cerrados. Seguir leyendo

items.title: EBOLA: Genomics links Nigeria’s case to Kenya index case – Pate
items.description: …says no evidence yet of direct travel link By Chioma Obinna Genomic analysis has revealed a close relationship between the Ebola virus detected in Nigeria’s confirmed case and the virus identified in the index case in Kenya, raising fresh questions about the connection between the infections as health authorities intensify containment measures. Read Also: Return of Ebola: Triumph of 2014, test of 2026 The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, who disclosed this on Friday night, however, stressed that there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan index case had travelled to Nigeria. He cautioned against drawing premature conclusions from the findings, explaining that genetic relatedness alone did not establish how the infection reached Nigeria. “We still have only one confirmed case. The contacts have been traced, quarantined, and we are conducting additional tests, some of which are negative and others are pending,” Pate said. He added that further genomic analysis could provide more information about the relationship between the viruses, although it might not necessarily resolve the route of transmission. He said the findings were made possible through the laboratory infrastructure of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and research facilities led by Professor Christian Happi at Redeemer’s University, Ede, Osun State. “That case appears to be closely related to the case identified in the index case in Kenya,” Pate said. The minister said the government was sustaining contact tracing, laboratory testing, surveillance and case management to prevent further transmission. He added that health authorities were also strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities. As part of the response, he said, health workers would receive training to improve their ability to identify suspected cases, protect themselves and promptly notify public health authorities. “All hospitals should be sensitised and health workers be aware and, when there are suspected cases, to notify public health authorities,” he said. Pate urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but calm, emphasising that Ebola was not transmitted through the air but through direct contact with the body fluids of an infected person. “Ebola is a disease that is so far not transmitted through airborne. It’s transmitted through close contact with body fluids,” he said. He advised the public to rely on information from the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the World Health Organisation and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, rather than unverified reports circulating on social media. The government is also developing and refining guidelines for mass gatherings in public spaces as part of efforts to protect public health while allowing activities to continue in line with evidence and established best practices. Pate said the measures formed part of a broader response involving the NCDC, the ministry, laboratories and public health professionals. Speaking, NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, said the agency would provide regular public briefings to explain the response, communicate preventive measures and encourage Nigerians to take practical steps to reduce the risk of infection. Idris stressed the importance of environmental control, personal hygiene and handwashing, recalling the preventive practices adopted during Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola outbreak. “It’s a contact issue. So, we need to address the issue of environmental control, personal hygiene, and hand washing,” he said. He said containing the disease required cooperation between government agencies, healthcare workers and the public, adding that regular updates would help Nigerians understand the situation and their role in preventing transmission. The government urged Nigerians to report suspected cases promptly, observe public health guidance and avoid spreading unverified information. Pate said the country remained vigilant and would continue to provide updates as testing and contact-tracing activities progressed. “There is no need to panic, but it is important to follow public health preventive measures that have been clearly identified,” he said. items.title: How 25-yr-old Ogun farmer died in police cell; family, community demand answers
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta What began as a routine arrest over an alleged petty theft of plantain has ended in tragedy, leaving a grieving family and the entire community of Ipara in Remo North Local Government Area of Ogun State demanding answers from the police. Read Also: Full List: Names of 37 miners who died in NSCDC custody Peter Igbang, a 25-year-old farmer and former mechanic apprentice, was pronounced dead in police custody. Police authorities claim he hanged himself inside the cell using his own clothing. His family and local leaders, however, have raised serious questions over the circumstances surrounding his death, the delayed notification of relatives, and conflicting accounts given by officers. Peter was arrested on Saturday, October 17, following an allegation that he stole a bunch of plantain. Relatives and community members described him as an industrious young man who owned a six-acre farm planted with cassava and mature plantain crops. Despite the arrest, his family said they received no formal notification for four days. Under Nigerian law, suspects are expected to be charged to court within 24 to 48 hours. That did not happen. “I have no other son” – Mrs. Gift Joseph, Mother Peter’s mother, Mrs. Gift Joseph, said she only learnt of her son’s arrest the day after his death, which was Tuesday, October 20. “Honestly, I do not know what to say. It was only Tuesday, October 20, that I heard my son had been arrested on Saturday. Nobody called me or informed me about what had happened,” she said. “My son had gone to the farm and was arrested on the road while returning. What I want to ask is this: in all my life, I have never seen or heard of someone being arrested and taken to a police station without their clothes being removed when they moving the person inside a cell, only for him to be left fully clothed and then reportedly hang himself inside the station. I find it difficult to understand how such a thing could happen. “I have no other son; he is my only son. I want the authorities to hear my questions and listen to what I have to say so that I can receive answers and have some peace of mind.” Gift confirmed that Peter was about 25 years old. Though trained as a mechanic, the family could not complete his apprenticeship or set up a workshop for him, so he turned to farming on his own six-acre land. Sister’s account of confusion and contradiction Peter’s elder sister, Juliet, who lives in Lagos with their mother and other siblings, said she received the shocking news on the evening of Tuesday, October 20, that the young man has died. “Yesterday evening (Tuesday, October 20), around 7 or 8 o’clock, I got a call from someone in Ogun State close to my brother saying that my brother had died,” Juliet recalled. “She said they arrested him on Saturday October 17, for stealing plantain. I asked how the family did not hear about it.” According to Juliet, a local woman who visited Peter in the cell said he complained of hunger and lack of water or food since Saturday, October 17, that he was arrested. He had pleaded that his family be contacted so he could be bailed. When Juliet and her mother finally reached the station on Wednesday , October 21, an officer’s first words were: “I’m sorry for your loss.” “I asked, ‘Loss? How?’ They said my brother hung himself. I said I wanted to see the cell. Is there a rope there? What is inside that cell that he could use to hang himself? They said he used his own clothes. “I asked, ‘But I thought when they arrest someone, they don’t allow them to go in with clothes except boxers. How come he was with his clothes?’ When they showed me a picture of him hanging on the window, he was wearing his full trousers. That means the boy was fully dressed. “They took me to the cell. I saw a small window that is very high. I asked how he got up there. They said he used a bucket. I asked what the bucket was doing inside the cell. They said it is normally in the bathroom beside the cell. “The story is just somehow. I am confused. I still don’t know what to do.” Community leaders dispute police claims Mr. Fidelis, former Chairman of Ogoja community in Ipara, said police only contacted him after Peter was already dead. “Yesterday they called me. When I reached the station, the man said something had happened. He opened the cell and I saw that Peter had hanged himself, with a rope around his neck, from the window,” Fidelis said. He said, “nobody called me until Peter died. Even me and the complainant have never seen each other. We don’t know each other.” Mr. Joseph, current chairman of the community, questioned both the detention procedure and the official explanation. “The question we asked at the station was: ‘Should a person be detained inside the station with his clothes?’ They said yes. But the way they showed us inside there, it does not look like the guy hanged himself. “What shocks me is that the man was arrested since Saturday. According to the law, after 24 hours you should charge the person to court. From Saturday to Tuesday, none of the family was aware. And the person they claimed was aware said they did not call him.” Another community member, Monday Philip, said he approached the complainant shortly after the arrest to plead for leniency. “I went to the man who arrested the Peter to beg him. He said he just wanted the boy to go there and learn a lesson for only one month and come back. I hadn’t even finished talking when the man kicked his motorcycle and left me standing there.” Calls for thorough investigation The family and community leaders insisted that the circumstances of Peter’s death must be thoroughly investigated, especially the decision to leave a detainee fully clothed, the presence of a bucket that could serve as a platform, the failure to notify next of kin promptly, and the claim that the young man said he had no family.
