items.title: Tenkodogo : Un crocodile capturé près d’un poulailler et relâché dans le barrage
items.description: Un crocodile qui rôdait près d’un poulailler dans une cour du quartier Gommisi, en face du Groupement de gendarmerie de Tenkodogo, a été capturé sans incident le jeudi 22 octobre 2026, puis relâché dans le barrage de la ville. L’alerte a été donnée par un habitant qui s’est présenté aux services compétents après avoir aperçu le reptile dans la concession. Aussitôt saisis, les agents du Service départemental des Eaux et Forêts (SDEF) de Tenkodogo, appuyés par la Brigade des Eaux et Forêts du Nakambé, se sont rendus sur les lieux. Selon la Direction régionale des Eaux et Forêts du Nakambé, l’animal a été maîtrisé dans le respect des mesures de sécurité, puis relâché dans le barrage de Tenkodogo. Aucun dégât n’a été constaté. L’intervention souligne l’importance de la vigilance citoyenne à proximité des points d’eau. Les Eaux et Forêts rappellent qu’il ne faut pas s’approcher ni tenter de capturer un animal sauvage, mais signaler immédiatement sa présence aux services compétents. items.title: 21-year-old butcher stabs colleague’s to death in Ogun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 21-year-old butcher, Selim Ayodele, over the alleged stabbing to death of his 26-year-old colleague, Ibrahim Wasiu, following a disagreement at their workplace in Alagbole, Ogun State. Read Also: Family seeks justice as butcher hacks 25-year old wife to death in Ekiti The incident reportedly occurred on Sunday, October 18, 2026, after the two men had finished work at a cow meat-selling outlet. In a statement issued on Friday, the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the incident was reported at the Ajuwon Police Station at about 8 p.m., prompting a police response. According to the police, preliminary investigations revealed that the disagreement between the two colleagues arose over who should sweep the floor after the day’s work. The statement alleged that during the ensuing altercation, Ayodele picked up a knife and stabbed Wasiu in the left side of his chest before twisting the weapon. The victim was subsequently rushed to Life Hospital, where he was confirmed dead on arrival. His remains were deposited at Life Channel Private Mortuary, Lanbe, Ajuwon, pending an autopsy, the police said. The police added that the suspect was in custody as investigations continued ahead of his prosecution. The Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to responding promptly to criminal incidents, conducting thorough investigations and ensuring the lawful prosecution of suspects. He also urged residents to exercise restraint when disagreements arise, resolve disputes peacefully and promptly report criminal incidents to the police. The command reiterated the importance of peaceful conflict resolution, warning against allowing minor disagreements to escalate into violence. The post 21-year-old butcher stabs colleague’s to death in Ogun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SIAO 2026 : Plus de 800 000 visiteurs attendus, des innovations majeures annoncées
items.description: Le président du comité d’organisation de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), Alassane Ouédraogo, a annoncé vendredi lors d’une conférence de presse que plus de 800 000 visiteurs sont attendus à la biennale de l’artisanat, prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, avec notamment plusieurs innovations. Ouagadougou, 23 oct. 2026 (AIB)- Le président du comité d’organisation de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), Alassane Ouédraogo, a annoncé vendredi, lors d’une conférence de presse , que plus de 800 000 visiteurs et plus de 6 000 exposants sont attendus à la biennale de l’artisanat, prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, avec notamment plusieurs innovations. Le PCO Alassane Ouédraogo a soutenu qu’outre les visiteurs, les organisateurs prévoient la construction de 800 stands et l’accueil de plus de 6 000 exposants. La 18e édition compte réunir au moins 30 pays, plus d’une centaine d’acheteurs professionnels des cinq continents et mobiliser au moins 350 journalistes issus de 50 médias nationaux et internationaux. S’agissant des innovations de l’édition, l’organisation évoque la climatisation de tous les pavillons, l’augmentation du nombre de portes d’entrée et de sortie et la mise en place de « points i » pour orienter les visiteurs et centraliser les préoccupations des exposants. Un « Village du pays invité d’honneur » sera également créé, de même que des ateliers thématiques au Village artisanal de Ouagadougou (VAO) pour mieux faire connaître les métiers de l’artisanat, a-t-il affirmé. Le comité d’organisation a également annoncé des prix et distinctions dans plusieurs catégories, notamment le Grand Prix du Président du Faso, le prix du Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple, le prix de la créativité Thomas Sankara, le prix du ministre chargé de l’Artisanat et celui de l’Organisation pour le développement et la promotion de l’artisanat africain (ODEPA). Placée sous le haut patronage du chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, l’édition se déroulera sur le thème « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ». Pendant dix jours, le public pourra découvrir des expositions-ventes, le concours de la créativité au Pavillon Thomas Sankara, des rencontres d’affaires B to B, un séminaire sur le thème central, des compétitions entre artisans, la journée du pays invité d’honneur, des animations culturelles et artistiques, ainsi que la nuit des artisans méritants. Des activités sportives, dont une course cycliste le 24 octobre à 7 heures sur le boulevard des Tansoba et un cross populaire le 29 octobre, seront également au programme. Le président du CNO a lancé un appel à la mobilisation générale. Il a invité les artisans à présenter leurs meilleures créations et à conquérir de nouveaux marchés, exhorté les entreprises, les banques et les assurances à accompagner la manifestation, et sollicité l’appui des médias pour la promouvoir. Né de l’exposition-vente « Artisanat 84 », selon le camarade Ouédraogo, le SIAO a connu sa première édition du 20 au 27 février 1988 à la Maison du Peuple de Ouagadougou. Il s’est depuis imposé comme l’un des grands rendez-vous de l’artisanat africain. Le Ghana est annoncé comme pays invité d’honneur, tandis que le Mali et le Niger, membres de la Confédération de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), seront les pays invités spéciaux. items.title: Boulgou/Garango : une exciseuse condamnée à 24 mois avec sursis pour avoir mutilé une fillette de 9 ans
items.description: Le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Tenkodogo a condamné une exciseuse à vingt-quatre mois d’emprisonnement avec sursis et à une amende de cinq cent mille francs CFA, dont deux cents cinquante mille fermes. Elle avait pratiqué une mutilation génitale féminine (MGF) sur une fillette d’environ neuf ans à Garango, dans la province du Boulgou. Le jugement a été rendu lors des audiences foraines correctionnelles tenues du 13 au 15 octobre 2026 dans cette commune. Les faits remontent au mois d’août 2026. Selon les informations recueillies, la mère de la victime a conduit sa fille auprès de R. A., présentée comme exciseuse, pour lui faire subir une excision. À la suite de l’intervention, la fillette a présenté une importante hémorragie nécessitant une prise en charge médicale urgente. Elle a d’abord été admise au Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Garango, avant d’être évacuée au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Tenkodogo, où elle a été hospitalisée pendant près d’une semaine avant de se rétablir. Trois femmes ont été mises en cause dans cette affaire. Considérée comme l’auteure principale, l’exciseuse a été jugée selon la procédure de flagrant délit et reconnue coupable de pratique de MGF. La mère de la victime et une autre femme, poursuivies pour complicité, ont bénéficié d’une procédure de composition pénale. Chacune s’est acquittée d’une amende de cinq cent mille francs CFA. Au-delà du traitement judiciaire, ces audiences foraines, tenues au pied du mont Boulgou, ont été l’occasion de rappeler aux populations les conséquences néfastes des MGF sur la santé et l’intégrité physique des filles. L’hémorragie survenue dans cette affaire, qui a nécessité l’évacuation de la fillette, illustre les risques liés à cette pratique prohibée par la loi. À travers cette audience délocalisée, le TGI de Tenkodogo a ainsi associé la sensibilisation à sa mission de répression des infractions. items.title: Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute: Chief Justice orders transfer of case to Tamale over security fears
items.description: The Chief Justice has granted a request by defendants in the Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute to transfer their case from the High Court in Nalerigu to Tamale over security concerns. One of the defendants, Elijah Saan, told JoyNews that they feared for their lives if they travelled to Nalerigu to attend court. He said the defendants had received intelligence suggesting they could be killed if they appeared in court in Nalerigu and had instructed their lawyer to apply for the transfer of the case to Tamale. The case was scheduled for hearing on Friday, October 23, 2026. The Registrar of the Nalerigu High Court confirmed to JoyNews on Friday that the Chief Justice had granted the request. The transfer comes amid heightened tensions in Bunkpurugu following the disputed enskinment of Melchizedek Musah Jamung as chief on September 14, 2026. The installation, which took place amid an ongoing chieftaincy dispute, reportedly triggered violence that left a woman dead and four others injured. Police have since been searching for the rival chief and other members of the Jamong royal family in connection with the disputed enskinment. The development has also prompted the Overlord of the Mamprugu Traditional Area, Naa Bohagu Abdulai Mahami Sheriga, to file an application at the High Court in Nalerigu seeking to have four people committed for contempt of court over the installation. In the application filed on October 14, 2026, the Nayiri accused the respondents of defying judicial processes by proceeding with the enskinment despite an ongoing legal dispute over the Bunkpurugu skin. The dispute between the Jamong and Jafouk royal families has contributed to persistent tensions in the area, with reports of farm destruction, arson and residents fleeing their homes amid fears of further violence.

items.title: Why crashes on Otedola Bridge — Lagos govt
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has absolved Otedola Bridge of any structural or engineering defects, attributing the recurring fatal crashes on the corridor to reckless driving, driver indiscipline, and overloaded heavy-duty trucks. The State Commissioner for Transportation, Mr. Oluwaseun Osiyemi, made the remark during the annual media parley organised by the Lagos State Ministry of Transportation held at Ikeja. The parley formed part of the updates presented by transportation agencies at the media parley, with officials outlining plans to improve public transport capacity, strengthen road safety, expand water transportation and make vehicle-related services more accessible. ​Refuting public speculation regarding the safety of the bridge’s design, Osiyemi revealed that a joint inspection conducted by team leads from both the Federal Ministry of Works and the Lagos State Government confirmed the integrity of the structure. “Our recent joint assessment with the Federal Controller of Works in Lagos, alongside previous structural integrity tests, shows conclusively that Otedola Bridge has no engineering defects. “The recurring accidents are largely linked to motorist behavior and the poor condition of vehicles plying the road,” Osiyemi stated. Addressing the menace of unroadworthy and overloaded articulated trucks, Osiyemi expressed concern over indiscriminate parking along major corridors, noting that such practices obstruct traffic flow and endanger lives. ​To curb infrastructure degradation and enhance road safety, the commissioner announced plans to deploy weighbridges across strategic locations in the state. The weighbridges will monitor truck weights and enforce compliance with legal limits. ​Osiyemi also warned motorists against speeding on corridors currently under construction, specifically highlighting the ongoing coastal road project. He urged drivers not to treat active construction zones as high-speed expressways and advised patience to prevent avoidable collisions. ​The state government reaffirmed that reducing road fatalities will require a multi-faceted approach combining driver discipline, stricter enforcement of traffic regulations, vehicle roadworthiness checks, and the upcoming weighbridge monitoring system. ​Also speaking at the parley, the General Manager of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Olalekan Bakare-Oki, stressed the enormous pressure commercial transportation places on the state’s road infrastructure. ​Bakare-Oki noted that over 60 per cent of all cargo transported in Nigeria originates from or moves through Lagos, resulting in heavy articulated truck traffic. “While indiscriminate movement and congestion caused by heavy-duty vehicles significantly accelerate road wear and increase crash risks, human error and excessive speeding remain the leading causes of crashes along the Otedola Bridge corridor,” he said. Recall that there have been incessant road crashes on the Otedola bridge along Lagos Ibadan Expressway, which often results into avoidable loss of lives and property. Consequently, motorists and residents have called on both Federal and State Governments’ intervention for a lasting solution that would address the situation. items.title: Over 500 ‘illegal’ Afghans held in three provinces
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Undocumented Afghan nationals continue to be arrested by authorities, and a joint report of IOM and UNHCR says over the past one week, 517 Afghans were arrested from three districts of Balochistan, Sindh and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Out of all arrests and detentions during October 11 to 17, ACC holders and undocumented Afghans from Chagai, Peshawar and Karachi represented 97 per cent of the total arrests and detentions, while Proof of Regis­tration (POR) holders represented 3 per cent. About 56pc of the total reported arrests and detentions took place in Balochistan, 34pc in Pun­jab and 10pc in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The report says prior to 2023, there was no data collected on the arrest and detention of Afghan Citizen Card (ACC) holders or undocumented Afghan nationals. Since January 2023, IOM has started to collect the data. Findings of the report show cumulatively, from Sept 15, 2023 to Oct 17, 2026, about 2,744,068 Afghans have been sent back to their country from Pakistan. Between Oct 11 and 17, UNHCR and IOM estimate 3,883 Afghans returned through the Torkham, Chaman and Bahramcha border crossing points to Afghanistan. Between October 11 and 17, the nu­­mber of returns decreased by 10pc and deportations by 48pc — compared to the previous week of October 4 to 10, 2026 (4,295 returns including 961 deportations). Betw­een Oct 11 and 17, a total of 3,883 returns were reported, including 499 deportations. Compared to the previous week, dep­o­­rtations de­­c­­reased significantly, while returns de­­creased only moderately, report says. Among those who returned bet­we­en Oct 11 and 17, most were un­­documented (83pc) followed by ACC holders (9pc) and PoR holders (8pc). Majority of the PoR returns were processed by UNHCR through the Volu­n­tary Repatriation Centres (VRCs). Among those deported between Oct 11 and 17, most were undocumented (99pc) followed by PoR holders (1pc) and ACC holders (1pc). Since April 1, 2025, 1,890,035 Afghans returned, of which 237,387 (13pc) were deported. During the period, fear of arrest remained the main reason for return among undocumented individuals and ACC holders (95pc) as well as for PoR holders (68pc). Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Tenkodogo : deux femmes accusées d’avoir traité d’autres personnes de sorcières devant le juge
items.description: Le tribunal de Tenkodogo a libéré deux femmes, A. Y. et B. B, faute de preuves. La justice leur reprochait d’avoir accusé d’autres personnes de sorcellerie. Dans cette affaire, c’est le procureur qui a demandé que les deux femmes soient libérées. Devant les juges, A. Y. a dit qu’elle n’avait rien fait. La personne qui se plaignait a même reconnu qu’A. Y. n’était pas là au moment des faits et qu’elle n’était pas responsable. Son nom avait été cité après une ancienne dispute, mais personne n’a pu dire ce qu’elle avait fait exactement. Le procureur a donc estimé qu’il n’y avait pas de faute et a demandé sa libération. Pour B. B., le tribunal a parlé d’un message audio. Dans ce message, une personne était accusée d’avoir rendu un enfant malade par la sorcellerie. Cette personne soupçonnait B. B., parce qu’elles avaient des problèmes entre elles et parce que des rumeurs circulaient. Mais elle n’avait aucune preuve. B. B. a affirmé qu’elle n’avait ni enregistré ni partagé ce message. La personne qui se plaignait a même dit qu’elle ne reconnaissait pas la voix entendue dans l’audio. Comme personne ne pouvait savoir qui avait enregistré le message, le procureur a demandé que B. B. soit libérée, au bénéfice du doute. Le procureur a tout de même averti sévèrement les deux femmes de ne plus jamais recommencer ce genre de choses. items.title: Farancis Duru: Meet the baby-faced legend of Nollywood
items.description: By Benjamin Njoku & Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Nigerian movie industry has been thrown into mourning again as popular actor, Francis Duru, has passed away at the age of 57 . Duru died following a brief illness, according to a statement released by his family in the early hours of Friday on his official Instagram page. “We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen,” the statement read. Confirming the sad news, the National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Sanusi Yakubu, posted Duru’s photograph with the caption: “Another great thespian gone… Rest in peace Francis Duru!!” Yakubu disclosed that the late actor was not diagnosed with any underlying ailment at the time of his death. According to him, Duru slipped into a coma three days ago, regained consciousness, but slipped back into coma on Thursday and did not survive. Duru’s close friend and colleague, Charles Inojie, also expressed shock in an Instagram post, writing: “Since the sad news of your untimely passing broke, I have lived in denial of the obvious reality, hoping against hope.” “Hold up the emblem of our common artistic ancestry until we meet again as cast of Thespis final production on Hallelujah day,” Inojie wrote. Veteran actor Kanayo O. Kanayo described Duru as one of the most flexible and prolific performers Nigeria ever produced. On his own part, showbiz promoter, Opa Williams, recalled how his path crossed with the late Francis Duru several years ago. Williams noted that apart from featuring in some of his earlier movies, Duru personally pasted posters for the first edition of his comedy franchise, “Nite of a Thousand Laughs”, in Port Harcourt in 1997 and served as anchor and foot soldier for the show in Abuja from 1999 to 2002. However, President Bola Tinubu has extended his heartfelt condolences to his family, colleagues, fans and the Nigerian film industry. The President in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga described the loss of the respected actor as a painful moment for Nollywood and the nation’s creative community, which has benefited immensely from its pioneers’ dedication, talent, and contributions. He acknowledges the important role veteran actors like Duru played in the growth and development of Nigeria’s film industry, particularly in shaping its artistic identity, nurturing emerging talent, and projecting Nigerian stories, culture, and values to audiences at home and abroad. In a condolence message, the National Film and Video Censors Board (NFVCB) described him as “a trained thespian whose career personified the pinnacle of discipline, artistry, and professional integrity.” “From his timeless breakout performance as Ahanna in the classic “Rattlesnake” (1995) to his extensive contributions across generations of Nollywood, Duru consistently championed content that balanced high aesthetic value with profound societal morality. “As a regulatory body committed to the growth and classification of quality films, the NFVCB recognizes Francis Duru as a thoroughbred professional who elevated the craft of acting. His strict adherence to artistic excellence on-screen and his constructive roles in industry leadership, including his service to the Actors Guild of Nigeria, helped shape the positive trajectory of Nollywood. “His recognition as a United Nations Ambassador of Peace further highlighted his commitment to using his creative platform for the betterment of society. Nigeria has lost a brilliant cultural ambassador and a rare standard-bearer for quality production,” the Board said. Similarly, the Nigerian Film Corporation,NFC, described the late actor as one who loved the art, noting that he was “a thespian with a difference” who loved sharing his career experiences as a speaker, anchor and discussant across various film industry platforms, universities and institutions, including the residency programme of the National Film Institute,NFI, Jos. “Beyond the deep and irreparable loss that his death will have on family members, relatives and friends, we will continue to remember and reference him for his lofty contributions to the growth and development of our film industry. He was indeed a resource and screen star, but sadly, cut down by death,” the NFC said. His death comes just weeks after legendary actor Olu Jacobs was laid to rest in Lagos, and months after Duru himself had debunked viral reports claiming he was battling a life-threatening illness. In June, footage showing him looking frail circulated widely on social media, sparking concern among fans and colleagues. In response, he shared an Instagram video describing the footage as “fabricated and malicious.” It was not the first time he had been the subject of false death rumours. On September 17, Duru had paid tribute to the late Olu Jacobs, describing him as a true and thorough-bred thespian who left footprints of professionalism, discipline and utmost dedication. Born on July 27, 1969, in Cameroon to Nigerian parents from Imo State, Duru had his primary and secondary education in Cameroon before relocating to Nigeria for his university education. He studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, graduating with a B.A. in 1996. He began his acting career in 1989 with “Missing Mark” directed by the late Ndubuisi Oko, but rose to prominence in 1995 after playing Ahanna in the action-comedy “Rattlesnake” produced by the late Amaka Igwe. Over a career spanning more than three decades, Duru became one of Nollywood’s most respected faces, featuring in numerous films including “Blood Money”, “Mboputa” and many others. He was honoured as a United Nations Ambassador of Peace in 2007 for his positive influence on youths. In 2020, he won Best Actor in a Leading Role (Igbo) at the Best of Nollywood Awards for his performance in “Mboputa.” He also served as interim President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria in 2010. Duru married his wife, Adokiye, in 2003 and they had four children. The family lost one of their children, Ifeanyi, in August 2024. Vanguard News The post Farancis Duru: Meet the baby-faced legend of Nollywood appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Violence threatening polls – ‘Tinubu must come’, ‘Tinubu must go’ supporters clash
items.description: *Parties lament raging danger to members’ lives *From Lagos to Enugu, Edo, Rivers, Kogi, Adamawa, meetings, rallies under attack *Opposition alleges killings, gunfire, assaults, destruction of party offices *INEC activates early-warning mechanism; reputation experts warn of investment losses *2023 election violence haunts preparations for next polls By Clifford Ndujihe & John Alechenu WITH the 2027 general elections approaching, political violence, threats and hate speech are raising fresh concerns about the safety of politicians, party members and voters, as rival camps increasingly accuse one another of using intimidation to gain electoral advantage. Read Also: * 2027: Outrage over Borno commissioner’s threat to flog non-APC supporters * 2027: Violence looms as politicians threaten voters, opponents across nation * Amnesty seeks action over Edo APC chairman’s AK-47 threat From Lagos to Enugu, Edo, Rivers, Kogi, Cross River, Adamawa and other parts of the country, political parties have reported attacks on meetings, rallies, campaign facilities and supporters, while allegations of threats against political opponents have intensified the atmosphere of apprehension ahead of the polls. In Lagos, more than 100 suspected hoodlums reportedly invaded the Labour Party,LP, secretariat at Idimu, Alimosho LGA, during a defection ceremony involving members moving to the African Democratic Congress, ADC. Furniture and party flags were destroyed, while members sustained injuries. When the gathering relocated to Eco Centre Hall in Egbeda, it was reportedly attacked again. In Enugu, gunmen allegedly disrupted political gatherings, while opposition parties in Kogi said attacks on ward meetings left members hospitalised. In Rivers, the ADC reported the killing of a member preparing for a political meeting. In Cross River, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, alleged that gunmen attacked two consultation venues, injuring three people. The violence has also touched gatherings associated with the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. In May, violence reportedly erupted during the party’s House of Assembly primary in Kosofe, Lagos, while vehicles belonging to PDP members were vandalised at a candidate affirmation event in Bauchi. In Adamawa, supporters of President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, associated with the slogan “Tinubu Must Come”, reportedly clashed with members of the opposing “Tinubu Must Go” movement during a rally in the Jimeta axis of Yola. The incidents, spanning different parties and regions, raise questions about the capacity of security agencies to protect political activities, investigate attacks impartially and prevent local disputes from escalating into wider violence. The concerns extend beyond party leaders. Lawyers, journalists, civil society groups, traditional rulers and election officials have warned that intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric could undermine public confidence in the electoral process. Pattern of attacks across states At a press conference in Abuja on September 22, the ADC said it had documented attacks and intimidation involving its members in at least nine states between July 2025 and September 2026: Kaduna, Kebbi, Ekiti, Cross River, Rivers, Edo, Osun, Kogi and Enugu. The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, cited attacks on party gatherings, assaults on members and threats allegedly directed at opposition politicians. In February, according to the ADC, the party’s secretariat in Benin City, Edo State, was attacked during a political gathering. Gunfire was also reportedly heard at the residence of former Edo State governor and former APC National Chairman, Chief John Odigie-Oyegun, where political leaders had assembled. The Edo State Police Command confirmed the incident and ordered an investigation. The ADC complained that no arrests, prosecutions or public report had followed at the time of its statement. In Rivers State, the party alleged that a member identified as Kamadiyoi was killed in Community Ward 1, Abua/Odual Local Government Area, while preparing for a meeting. In Enugu State, an opposition gathering was reportedly disrupted by armed men, with police confirming that a man sustained a gunshot injury. The state government disputed claims that a life had been lost in the incident. The ADC also cited the disruption of an NDC gathering at Akanu Ibiam International Airport, where supporters had assembled to receive their governorship candidate. The government said the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria’s permission had not been obtained for the gathering. The Enugu chapter of the ADC, through the Obodoeze Media Project, described the reported use of firearms in a political environment as a serious threat to public safety and demanded a thorough, impartial investigation. Three opposition governorship candidates in the state — Uche Nnaji of the PDP, Christian Ohaa of the NDC and Ozor Obodoeze Ocho of the ADC — jointly demanded an independent investigation by the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, with substantial representation from outside the Enugu State Police Command. Timeline of attacks, clashes, disruptions May–October 2026 1. Date : May 18, 2026 Location : Osogbo, Osun Incident and reported impact : Accord alleged that armed men attacked Governor Ademola Adeleke’s campaign office and the party secretariat, damaging windows and offices. 2. Date : May 21, 2026 Location : Kosofe, Lagos Incident and reported impact : Violence marred the APC House of Assembly primary at Ikosi Senior High School. Supporters of aspirant Femi Saheed alleged that armed hoodlums attacked members, leaving several injured. 3. Date : May 26, 2026 Location : Bauchi Incident and reported impact : Suspected political thugs vandalised vehicles belonging to PDP members at a governorship candidate affirmation event. 4. Date : June 9, 2026 Location : Ile-Ife, Osun Incident and reported impact : A campaign walk for APC governorship candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, reportedly degenerated into violence around Sabo, leaving about three people injured. 5. Date : July 31, 2026 Location : Ezza South, Ebonyi Incident and reported impact : Thugs attacked a PDP rally organised for Ifeanyi Nworie. About 10 members were reportedly injured, while canopies, chairs and public-address equipment were destroyed. 6. Date : August 30, 2026 Location : Kuje, FCT Incident and reported impact : An Accord Party gathering was reportedly attacked by suspected thugs armed with cutlasses. Participants fled, property was damaged and at least one person was reportedly injured. 7. Date : September 9, 2026 Location : Kaduna Incident and reported impact : ADC supporters on a solidarity walk for governorship candidate, Isa Ashiru, were reportedly attacked by suspected thugs. 8. Date : September 12, 2026 Location : Nkanu West, Enugu Incident and reported impact : An NDC ward meeting at Ndiuno-Obuoffia was reportedly disrupted by gunmen, leaving two attendees injured. Canopies and chairs prepared for a separate PDP rally at Agbani were also reportedly destroyed. Police ordered an investigation. 9. Date : September 14, 2026 Location : Isiokpo, Rivers Incident and reported impact : An ADC meeting in Ikwerre LGA was reportedly disrupted by suspected political thugs. 10. Date : September 15, 2026 Location : Ejule, Kogi Incident and reported impact : Suspected thugs reportedly disrupted an ADC meeting in Ofu LGA. The party also alleged attacks on members preparing for meetings in two wards, with several people hospitalised. 11. Date : Mid-September 2026 Location : Abua/Odual, Rivers Incident and reported impact : The ADC alleged that a member identified as Kamadiyoi was killed while party members prepared for a meeting in Emilaghan community, Ward 1. The attackers’ identities were not independently established. 12. Date : October 2, 2026 Location : Calabar South, Cross River Incident and reported impact : The PDP alleged that gunmen attacked two consultation venues, injured three people and vandalised supporters’ vehicles. 13. Date : October 6, 2026 Location : Igueben, Edo Incident and reported impact : The ADC alleged that gunmen attacked a campaign convoy involving Kenneth Imasuangbon and Herbert Okonofua, leaving supporter Jerry Oliha with gunshot wounds. An accused APC-linked council chairman denied involvement. 14. Date : October 14, 2026 Location : Jimeta, Adamawa Incident and reported impact : A rally supporting Tinubu’s second-term ambition reportedly encountered opposition from “Tinubu Must Go” supporters. *The list is not exhaustive. The ADC has also cited alleged attacks and intimidation in Kebbi and Ekiti. Threats from political podiums Beyond physical attacks, statements attributed to public officials and political actors have raised concerns about the atmosphere in which parties are expected to campaign. In Esan West Local Government Area of Edo State, the council chairman was accused of threatening to demolish hotels that hosted NDC meetings. He was also alleged to have visited Ekpoma motor park and directed that commercial drivers wearing the caps of other parties be barred. In Kuje Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory, Chairman Danjuma Shekwolo was accused of telling residents who would not vote for the APC to leave the council. In Borno State, a commissioner was reportedly accused of threatening to cut off the fingers of people who refused to support the APC. In Osun, a senator was reported to have urged supporters to “kill” Accord Party members ahead of the governorship election. These allegations raise serious questions about the responsibilities of public officials and the protection of citizens’ political rights. In Rivers State, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, warned that former governor Rotimi Amaechi “will find it difficult to campaign in Rivers” if he continued describing President Tinubu and his supporters as thieves. The ADC’s Abdullahi warned against the politicisation of law enforcement. “The Nigeria police is not APC police; it is the police of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. South-East tensions Elder statesman and Chairman of the Igbo Agenda Dialogue, Chief Chekwas Okorie, warned South-East governors against allowing the region to become a theatre of political conflict. “It is no longer safe for members of opposition parties to hold public gatherings anywhere in the geopolitical zone without being attacked by heavily armed thugs,” he said. Okorie also accused some governors of charging hundreds of millions of naira for a single campaign billboard, a practice he said could restrict opposition parties’ access to public spaces. He alleged that some opposition groups had responded by tearing down ruling-party billboards. In Enugu, Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, accused opposition members of plotting to bring thugs and bandits into the state. He said the government would not allow a national asset such as the airport to be converted into a campaign ground. The competing claims underscore the need for security agencies to distinguish legitimate security concerns from restrictions that could prevent lawful political activity. Lessons from Lagos in 2023 Nigeria’s experience during the 2023 general elections offers a warning about the possible consequences of intimidation, identity-based rhetoric and attacks on political opponents. The Centre for Democracy and Development, which deployed observers across all 36 states, reported that intimidation linked to identity or party affiliation occurred in 3.4 per cent of polling units. Lagos, Anambra and Imo featured prominently in its findings. On February 25, 2023, videos from Surulere, Lagos, showed young men overturning tables, removing ballot boxes marked “Presidential” and smashing them on the road along Adedoyin Road. Ballot papers were scattered into gutters, and INEC later cancelled results in four polling units, affecting 1,950 registered voters. PDP House of Representatives candidate for Surulere Constituency I, Alani Jeje, popularly known as Bobby Jeje, alleged that thugs moved from one polling unit to another, beating voters. “They have beaten up people in areas where PDP is very strong. They are doing this right under the watch of the police,” he said. Actress Chioma Akpotha also said she was attacked at her polling unit. “They destroyed everything including my car side mirrors. I had to run out,” she wrote. The atmosphere deteriorated further before the March 18 governorship election, when a video of Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, circulated online. He was heard warning a woman identified as Iya Chukwudi: “If you don’t want to vote for us, stay at home.” Police urged Nigerians to treat the statement as a joke. On election day, the European Union Election Observation Mission reported that at least 21 people were killed nationwide. Its Chief Observer, Barry Andrews, identified Lagos as one of the worst-affected states. In Oke-Afa, Ejigbo, armed men wearing party tags reportedly attempted to seize a Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, machine. In Okota, a suspected thug was shot by a policeman while allegedly attempting to snatch a ballot box, while another suspected thug was reported shot dead at Star Time Estate, Ago Palace Way. At Ijagemo, 10 people were reportedly injured when armed men on eight motorcycles invaded polling units. Further reports of intimidation and violence came from Ojo, Eti-Osa, Fadeyi, Ajegunle, Ajah, Festac, Somolu and Berger. The United States’ 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices said APC supporters in Ojo threatened Igbo voters and that non-Yoruba voters were blocked in Eti-Osa. The US Mission said its observers witnessed voter intimidation in Lagos. “The use of ethnically charged rhetoric before, during, and after the gubernatorial election in Lagos was particularly concerning,” the Embassy said. The then Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Idowu Owohunwa, acknowledged that violence had occurred but said it was “not as widespread as to affect the general dynamics.” Voter turnout, however, stood at 16 per cent, the lowest for a governorship election in the state’s history. Labour Party governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour later described the experience as a pattern of intimidation and voter suppression. “It’s a culture of violence, and intimidation and voter suppression, and I think that was the main obstacle for me in the 2023 elections,” he said. The absence of major convictions following many of the reported incidents remains a concern for advocates of electoral accountability. INEC’s early-warning system faces test Against this background, INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has warned political actors against allowing competition to descend into bloodshed. Speaking at a workshop for editors in Abuja, Amupitan said: “No political office in this country is worth the blood of a single Nigerian.” He said the commission had activated an early-warning framework through the Inter-Consultative Committee on Election Security, ICCES, to monitor violence, thuggery and hate speech. “INEC will not stand by and allow political competition to devolve into violence,” he warned. The commission also announced plans for joint financial-monitoring teams involving the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU. INEC said more than 10.6 million new voters had been registered and 57,000 new BVAS devices acquired. However, the effectiveness of the early-warning framework will depend on whether threats are identified promptly, security agencies act on credible information, and perpetrators face investigation and prosecution regardless of party affiliation. Monitoring alone may not prevent violence if warnings do not translate into timely deployments, protection for vulnerable gatherings and credible consequences for those who organise or finance attacks. Nigeria’s reputation at stake Chairman of the Board of the Nigeria Reputation Management Group, NRMG, Yomi Badejo-Okusanya, has warned that election-related insecurity could damage the country’s international standing and cost it investment opportunities. Speaking at Nigeria Reputation Day 2026, themed “Own the Narrative: Shaping Nigeria’s Reputation Together,” he disclosed that a prospective international investor cancelled a planned visit following a travel advisory linked to concerns about the forthcoming elections. “We must have these elections in a peaceful atmosphere. If you don’t win today, you can win tomorrow. It is not winning at all costs that we must all do,” he said. The warning highlights the wider cost of political violence: beyond injuries, deaths and damaged property, it can discourage investment, weaken confidence in public institutions and undermine the legitimacy of elected governments. As the 2027 elections approach, the challenge before INEC, the police, political parties and governments at all levels is to ensure that political competition remains peaceful, that citizens can attend meetings without fear, and that allegations of violence are investigated impartially. The experience in Lagos in 2023 shows the potential consequences when intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric go unchecked. The latest reports suggest that the warning signs are already visible. The central question is whether Nigeria’s institutions will act early enough to prevent the coming electoral contest from becoming another cycle of violence, fear and impunity. items.title: Ghana needs 759 million cedis to implement 2025-29 health sector supply chain master plan
items.description: More than 759 million cedis — that is how much Ghana needs to fix critical gaps in the supply of medicines and essential medical supplies across the country’s health facilities over the next four years. But with some foreign aid to the health sector being withdrawn, the government is turning to domestic resources to fund the plan and keep Ghana’s universal health coverage target for 2030 within reach. At the launch of the 2025-2029 health sector supply chain master plan, stakeholder say effective funding, improved financial management and the recovery of outstanding debts owed under the National Health Insurance Scheme will be crucial to ensuring that health facilities, particularly those serving women and children, have the essential commodities they need to save lives. The master plan is a revised version of the 2021 – 2025 plan which was partially implemented due to the COVID-19 outbreaks with 35% of the overall targets achieved. The old plan revealed significant gaps in the planning, governance, workforce and operation sectors for the effective rollout of health The new plan is aimed at ensuring the completion of critical tasks while enhancing supply chain adaptability and responsiveness to emerging challenged. The master plan encompasses forty-seven (47) strategic interventions, each linked to the annual performance targets across the second (II) technical areas. The plan seeks to ensure availability, timely-access, affordability of high-quality health commodities across public and private sectors to successfully deliver universal health coverage ensuring Ghanaians have access to high-quality health care services. Targets by 2029 The masterplan seeks to build an integrated central and regional medical stores distribution on time and in full for all service delivery points while tracking cost components. It will also develop a well-coordinated financial system that supports the public health system. The implementation of the masterplan will include a mapping exercise to understand the flow of money and tracking of expenditures at each level. Speaking at the launch of the masterplan in Kumasi, Director for Procurement and Supply Chain at the Ministry of Health, Dr. Edward Bright Agyekum, noted that the government remains focused on generating revenue locally for the masterplan’s implementation. This comes amidst withdrawal of some foreign aid to the health sector, but Dr. Agyekum says strategies are in place to mobilize resources locally to achieve key priorities set out under the plan. “The supply chain master plan will be implemented with local funds. We are using whatever we have to generate. Whatever we are going to do to ensure it’s a local funding, we are mobilizing the scarce resources, the government is pushing for it. We are doing, we are mindful that come what may, the donors will withdraw. We are raising local funding to support implementation,” he said. Owning the SCMP implementation Technical Director with the Global Health Supply Chain, Daniel Oswald Owusu Afranie says the country make be deliberate in owning the masterplan for a universal health coverage by 2030. “The development partners have supported in putting this together. But its implementation is something government must take over and plan towards that. Resource mobilizing is very key,” he said. He noted that the government must devise ways to recoup all debts incurred under the health insurance scheme to complement revenue mobilization for the implementation. He acknowledged that these huge arrears affect the operations of the medical supply stores in procuring and distributing health commodities to health facilities. “How does the NHIS come in. Because in terms of health financing which the NHIA is already doing. We have to look at what role they will be playing in the implementation of the supply chain masterplan. There must be practical measures to ensure those debts are collected so that the regional medical stores will be able to function as business entities,” he added. Focus on Women and Children Women and children are among the most vulnerable groups in Ghana’s healthcare system, with access to essential medicines, vaccines and other medical supplies playing a critical role in their survival and well-being. Supply and Procurement Manager at UNICEF, Honorine Niyomana, stressed that the plan must deliberately and strategically focus on women and children. Ms. Niyomana says inadequate supplies could hinder mother and children from accessing equitable care. “Ghana has made important progress in improving health for women and children. But progress can be lost quickly when the commodities run out. A stock out of a single essential medicine can send a mother or caregiver home without care or force a family to travel far or pay off out of pocket,” she said.

items.title: From power vandalism to gunrunning: Delta’s mammy market’s dark economy of powerline, arms
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi For years, the 3 Battalion Mammy Market, adjoining the Tomatoes Market in Effurun, Delta State, thrived as a bustling civilian settlement inside a military formation, home to traders, residents and all manners of hustle. On October 12, bulldozers rolled in. The demolition followed expiration of a 24-hour eviction notice issued two days earlier to civilian occupants and traders. For years, the space ahad been a source of discreet income to the Effurun Barracks authorities who allocate space for temporary structures occupied by squatters at negotiated fees and levies But behind the market’s commercial bustle, the authorities said, a darker economy had grown. The eviction which left thousands displaced was carried out to reclaim the land and address pressing security concerns. The real trigger, Vanguard gathered, was a formal complaint to the National Security Adviser in an October 9 letter by the Transmission Company of Nigeria, TCN, signed by its Managing Director/CEO, Dr. Sule Ahmed Abdulaziz. That letter has now exposed the Mammy Market as more than a market. It was, by TCN’s estimation, a safe haven for the new threat to national development – unrestrained vandalism of power infrastructure. In the petition titled REQUEST FOR SECURITY INTERVENTION ON THE VANDALIZATION OF TCN INSTALLATIONS IN SAPELE, TCN told the NSA it has been facing repeated vandalism of its installations around that axis and beyond, posing serious threat to power distribution. The company said its investigation traced the sabotage to hoodlums operating within and around the Mammy Market on the 3 Battalion grounds along Effurun-Sapele Road. TCN then solicited NSA intervention to direct Brigadier General I B Buhari to take necessary security measures to apprehend and remove the suspects. Abdulaziz wrote: “TCN has been experiencing a series of vandalism targeting its installations around the area of Delta State. These repeated attacks pose a serious threat to the reliability and security of electricity transmission infrastructure in the area. “In the course of our investigation, credible information was gathered indicating that hoodlums operating within and around the Mammy Market are responsible for the attacks and vandalization of TCN installations.” The letter was copied to the Director of Critical National Assets and Infrastructure Protection at the Presidency. The consequential raid ordered by the federal government revealed deeper than anticipated. Fighting one threat exposed another. Though the authorities are shy of talking about it, the military operation reportedly uncovered booming trade in gunrunning, hard drugs and brothels during the demolition. Security sources referenced 40 AK-47 rifles and other ammunition allegedly recovered, with some persons including the market leader reportedly arrested. Brigadier General Ibrahim Baba Buhari, Commander 63 Brigade Asaba and Commander Sector 1, South-South, Operation Delta Safe, was not forthcoming with official position. Neither was the Commanding Officer at the 3 Battalion. But top military sources who spoke behind camera gave insight into the underworld the Effurun Mammy had become. One senior officer explained the procedure for high-profile suspects when Vanguard sought response from relevant military formations in Delta. “If we have caught some people with rifles, that means they are high-profile suspects, right? And, in our mandate, they are not meant to stay with us for a very long time. As soon as we finish our investigation, we hand them over to police, is that so?” He added he was not directly in charge of the market: “I’m just hearing what you’re telling me now. I have to make my own findings also. Me, I’m in the Brigade, not in the sector. And the Mami Market is under the CO 3 Battalion, not under the Brigade or sector.” Another security source who monitored the demolition was more direct about what Mammy harboured: “The location is Uburoko, just right behind the Mami Market. Those are also inside the barracks, that’s where those brothels are, inside the Mammy. “So, that’s where they hide after vandalizing those pylons. So, that people lose electricity, and the national grid is down, it’s because of actions like this.” He said the adjoining scrap market is the real enabler that must be shut: “There’s a need for the scrap market to be scrapped. Otherwise, they are all looting to the scrap market, and the vandalization or vandalism will continue. “Government should close downthat scrap market, because nothing good ever happens out of a scrap market. They call those scrap markets ‘One Naija,’ ‘One Sambisa’. “Once they (stolen power line assets) enter there, under five minutes, they have it dismantled, it’s melted. They harbour them, you can’t separate good people from bad people.” He said vandalism started in December 2025 but became unbearable in August 2026 when 11 pylons were brought down after vandals cut smaller components to weaken the structure. One vandal died when a weakened tower collapsed on him. “That picture of the dead person, he didn’t know the pylon rods had become weak from initial scavenging. So as he was cutting the pipe, the thing just came down on him.” He warned eviction alone will not work because displaced vandals are relocating to a dump site across the road, stressing that police, NDLEA and other agencies find it difficult to enter Mammy because it is taken as a military zone. “The Police, NDLEA and other security agencies, they find it difficult to penetrate and enter (the Mammy) because they take it as a military zone so most of them (vandals) seek safe haven in Mammy.” He defended the operation was not a raid: “We were not even raiding. We were just demolishing. So they are entering, picking their things and leaving. We are not beating anybody, not restricting them.” He said TCN is exhausted by the cost and delay of replacement. “TCN got tired. The one in Delta cannot repair those pylons. They have to get it from outside and it takes months. Just compare the amount of energy being lost to vandals.” Visual evidence shows catastrophic damage – total structural failure of towers like T98 and T100 after systematic stripping of base bracing, angle iron, bolts and gusset plates. TCN’s patrol on Delta/Afisere 132kV line found nine towers – T9, T10, T11, T12, T14, T15, T16, T17 & T18 – vandalised and needing urgent rehabilitation to avoid collapse. Not An Isolated Case The pattern is not limited to Delta. In Rivers State, advocate Alhaji Brian Barile who documents vandalism from Afam Power Plant, Oyigbo to Elelenwon in Obio/Akpor said: “From Elelenwon to Oyigbo, all the base braces and components of the electricity towers are gone, all stolen.” He described what he met around Green City Estate: “I was on the railway from Elelewon to Ogba side doing some work when I decided to stroll within Elelewon, under the Green City Estate, around the designated International Cattle Market when I discovered the mind-boggling vandalism.” Comparing untouched and vandalised towers, he said, “I saw one (pylon) untouched because there are living houses surrounding. You can see it’s complete, untouched, formidable and giving the pylon strength to stand.” “Others have been compromised, vandalised. They’ve everything at the base removed and you can see the pole (mast) bending. Anything can happen now. The strength of these poles are gone.” For TCN, the bulldozers in Mammy were not just about land. It was a desperate push to save the national grid from a dark economy of scrap, arms and drugs thriving behind barracks gates. For the law-abiding among thousands of squatters evicted from the Mammy, the bulldozers also left in their trail huge human cost in loss of property and livelihoods many would take who knows how long to recover from. Vanguard News The post From power vandalism to gunrunning: Delta’s mammy market’s dark economy of powerline, arms appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: When Pete Edochie wept in Ghana
items.description: By Fred Iwenjora For legendary journalist, broadcaster, actor Chief Dr. Pete Edochie, MON, big honor seems to come from abroad as he just concluded a nine-day tour of Ghana. Read Also: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57 FRED IWENJORA reports that very brave Okonkwo of Things Fall Apart! Ebubedike, the Ononenyi of Nteje, Anambra state and Ibobo Oyi na Omambala shed tears uncontrollably during this tour especially when students and pupils of Knutsford University used his name for different forms of recitations and poetry. One may ask why Pete Edochie traveled to Ghana. This visit was for the launching of the Pete Edochie Legacy project, themed Celebrating the Africa legend; The lion that needs not to roar. It is “a cultural initiative created to honor and celebrate one of Africa’s most revered figures” according to the Ghanaian project organisers. The Legacy project includes a biographical book, a documentary series and international tour with Ghana serving as the launch pad. The publishers, KPL publishers had noted that the contributions of the 79 year old screen star to Africa cinema are very noteworthy. At the end of it all, the star actor had, aside unveiling his autobiography in a gala event, paid courtesy calls to industry and policy makers in Ghana including the visit to Ghana’s Goldbod, the body regulating everything gold in Ghana. Organisers saw the visit as an important segment of the tour because a visit to Ghana may have been incomplete without seeing first hand the reason the country was called Gold Coast. He had also met and greeted select fans and featured in a public lecture and colloquium in his honor before returning to Nigeria. From when he landed at Kotoka International Airport Tuesday 29th September, 2026 till his departure from Ghana on Wednesday 7, October 2026, there was no dull moment. Reception was top notch and indeed out of this world. Ghanaians as well as Nigerians left businesses and trouped out to see “the president of African screen” according to Elizabeth Ama Tetteh, one of his numerous Ghanaian fans who noted that she had been resident in Enugu, Nigeria. It was indeed heartwarming to see Ghanaian as well as Igbo cultural groups on hand to welcome him to the old Gold Coast. Dispatch riders led his motorcade out of the airport. On arrival, he first paid a courtesy visit to Eze Dr. Chukwudi Jude Ihenetu, Onyendu Ndi igbo, Ghana and sued for peace between Nigeria and Ghana. The respected Eze Ihenetu had organised a congregation of Igbo and Ghanaian leaders for a traditional cocktail reception. According to the major propeller of the project Kelvin King Dawie of King Dawie Publishing Ltd (KPL) “When people ask why Pete Edochie, I tell them that no honor for Pete Edochie is too big. He has very much distinguished himself on the continent of Africa and beyond as a custodian of the cultural heritage of Africa and has been consistent in it for decades since mounting the stage at the tender age of 15. He is well known and received a lot of honors and awards globally including Nigeria’s national honor of merit; MON. “We also looked at the way he has distinguished himself on stage and in communication which has warranted him receiving Honorary Doctorate in Literature and creative arts. On this continent, Pete Edochie is one of a kind and he needs to be projected and celebrated as that icon of Africa who has held high the heritage of Africa for over six decades of his acting life. King Dawie, an accountant, business strategist and social impact leader also hinted that “the project is in four phases, the autobiography, a 16-episode documentary to properly chronicle his life’s journey and then also the African youth mentorship initiative to help him pass on information to the next generation and an international tour. It took a lot of several efforts from several people too numerous to mention to set this ball rolling and hopefully achieving. We also remain very grateful to our star guest for accepting our proposal. ” However, there are major take-aways from these nine days Pete Edochie “Presidential visit” to Ghana. Cultural diplomacy at itshighest African peak Years back, Africa viewers had voted Pete Edochie as their main choice in (AMVCA). However, this Ghana visit is International cultural diplomacy at its highest African peak. It seems first in history that a film star would make so much impression in another country that a book would be written and unveiled on him in that country. It also reveals that Nigeria and Ghana have co-existed as West Africa’s beloved Anglophone countries despite hiccups occasioned by various ‘Ghana must go’ or ‘Nigeria must go’ agitations. And to see both Nigerians and Ghanaians under one roof because of Pete Edochie, animosities may have been doused even if for a moment. The unveiling of the autobiographical book; Titan of Africa, the story of Pete Edochie, published by KPL Publishers was a big attraction on its own and first of its kind for a Nigerian actor. The event which held at Kempiski Accra drew together distinguished Ghanaians with highlights including his meeting with Ghanaian legendary actress, broadcaster and musician Grace Omaboe, known to many as Maame Dokono. He also met with 102 years old Warrant Officer 1 and WW2 veteran, Pa Joseph Ashitey Hammond. Their tight hug meant that this meeting for the WW2 veteran was highly anticipated like the story of the nunc dimitis contained in the synoptics. These are pointers to the huge respect that he commands in the so called Gold Coast and that Africa is so culturally connected in many ways. Another take away from the tour was that the man Pete Edochie is very well blessed and his star never seems to dim as years roll by. Despite that he is bound to the wheelchair and could barely walk or sits on the chair in his current films, fans continue to adore him from far and near. The post When Pete Edochie wept in Ghana appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: RDC: une nouvelle étape franchie pour le projet d’organisation du référendum
items.description: En RDC, l’Assemblée nationale a adopté la loi fixant les conditions d’organisation du référendum ce vendredi 23 octobre sans l’opposition, après l’intégration des réserves formulées par la Cour constitutionnelle il y a trois mois. Le texte ouvre notamment la possibilité de modifier des dispositions constitutionnelles, y compris celles qui étaient verrouillées par l’article 220, voire d’adopter une nouvelle Constitution. Une perspective qui suscite de vives inquiétudes dans les rangs de l’opposition et de la société civile qui soupçonnent le président de chercher à rester au pouvoir.

items.title: Jordan church shooting claims 7 lives
items.description: AMMAN: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said, with the king vowing retaliation for the rare attack on Christians in the majority Muslim kingdom. Assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate and opened fire, authorities said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and started shooting during a funeral procession, the public security directorate said in a statement, adding that a manhunt was underway for the perpetrators. “The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation,” King Abdullah II said in a post on X. “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” According to images from state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka, the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening. After authorities gave a death toll of six, Director of Public Security Major General Abdullah Al-Maaytah said it had risen to seven with 34 injured, 27 of whom were still receiving treatment. Footage aired by Al-Mamlaka showed two gunmen dressed in casual clothes and brandishing pistols, with a third carrying a long gun as they opened fire on the church. A witness said the gunmen fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
items.description: The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key Senate race said she had lobbied for the change. Starting on 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said on Friday. Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state’s agriculture industry. The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August. Maine Senator Susan Collins is seeking to keep her seat in November’s midterm elections Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were “necessary to protect our workers”. Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs “dollar for dollar” after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called “unequal treatment” of US cars, dairy and alcohol. The White House said while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and “waste products”. It said the action reflected President Trump’s “continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade”. “President Trump continues to address Canada’s discriminatory treatment of US commerce,” White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said. In a statement to the BBC, Canada’s internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: “While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada’s interests.” The White House’s announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump’s Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term. Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would “continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally, and largest trading partner”. She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were “crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers”. Collins’ Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, responded: “Trump’s trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire.” Maine borders the Canadian provinces New Brunswick and Quebec. Its economy, as well as that of other border states, is deeply linked to Canada and they have felt the effects of the months-long trade war. Michigan lawmaker Mike Rogers, also a Republican, has called on Trump to end the standoff after spending months supporting the policy in recent advertisements airing in his trade-reliant state. Also on Friday, President Donald Trump said Canada was “working very hard” on a ⁠trade ​deal with the US. Carney, for his part, said that Canada was open to a mutually beneficial deal, but is willing to wait it out. “We could sign it this afternoon if the US were there. If it has to be months from now or longer than that, or another administration, before a proper deal comes into place, we will do that,” he said on Friday, according to Canadian broadcaster CBC. LeBlanc confirmed on Thursday that a delegation met with members of the Canada-United States Economic Relations Advisory Committee – the ninth meeting since April 2026. The committee members discussed the ongoing impact of US tariffs in Canada.

items.title: Burkina : la coupe du Faso s’ouvre désormais à 11 disciplines
items.description: Longtemps concentrée sur le football, la Coupe du Faso s’est maintenant ouverte à 11 autres disciplines dont les finales se disputeront les 24 et 25 octobre, a annoncé vendredi à Ouagadougou, la Directrice générale des sports et des loisirs Valérie Badolo/Tapsoba au cours d’une conférence de presse. La Directrice générale des sports et des loisirs Valérie Badolo/Tapsoba a donné les détails des modalités d’organisation de ces compétitions, soulignant que cette initiative du ministère des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi marque une nouvelle étape dans la valorisation des disciplines longtemps restées dans l’ombre du football. Pour cette première édition, onze disciplines sont concernées : l’athlétisme, les sports pour personnes handicapées, le volleyball, le handball, le rugby, la lutte, la boxe, la pétanque, le karaté-do, le taekwondo et le cyclisme. À travers ces compétitions, les autorités entendent diversifier l’offre sportive, améliorer la préparation des athlètes et favoriser la détection de nouveaux talents. L’initiative vise également à accroître la visibilité des disciplines concernées, à promouvoir l’équité sportive et à renforcer la cohésion sociale. Selon la directrice générale, cette première phase dont le budget est de 100 millions, pourrait être étendue à d’autres disciplines, en fonction des résultats obtenus, des ressources disponibles et de la capacité des fédérations à répondre aux exigences organisationnelles. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité d’une mobilisation coordonnée des fédérations sportives, des encadreurs, des athlètes et des partenaires pour garantir le bon déroulement des finales. Le respect des règlements, la discipline et le fair-play devront, selon elle, guider les compétitions. Mme Badolo/Tapsoba a, par ailleurs, invité les médias à assurer une couverture professionnelle et responsable de l’événement, afin de mieux faire connaître ces disciplines et de valoriser les performances des sportifs auprès du public. Inscrite dans la dynamique de promotion de la jeunesse et de valorisation des potentialités nationales, cette initiative ambitionne de faire du sport un vecteur de cohésion, de solidarité et de patriotisme. La directrice générale a souhaité que cette première édition ouvre la voie à une dynamique durable au bénéfice de l’ensemble du mouvement sportif burkinabè. Agence d’information du Burkina as/ata L’article Burkina : la coupe du Faso s’ouvre désormais à 11 disciplines est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: KP governor rules out talks with ‘anti-state elements’
items.description: • Kundi calls for decisive action against terrorists, stronger police capacity • Says Centre ready to provide weapons, financial resources to KP police • Insists peace essential for development, investment in province CHARSADDA / PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday ruled out negotiations or concessions for elements who do not accept the Constitution, stressing that decisive action against terrorism and strengthening the province’s police was the only way to restoring peace. Speaking to journalists after visiting the families of CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan and Constable Kazim Jan in Charsadda, Mr Kundi said elements working against the state should not be offered concessions. He said the Pakistan Army, police and other security agencies had rendered immense sacrifices for the country’s security and stressed that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa must be freed from terrorism. Referring to a recent meeting of the National Apex Committee , the governor said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had made it clear that a policy of zero tolerance would be adopted against terrorism. He said decisive action against terrorists was necessary to restore lasting peace, adding that the public should distance itself from terrorists and refrain from providing them shelter. Mr Kundi said police and other law enforcement agencies required modern weapons and equipment to confront terrorists and that he was prepared to divert funds from his development allocation for the purpose. He added that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had assured him that the federal government was ready to provide the police with the required weapons and financial resources. Mr Kundi said the compensation package for police personnel martyred in the line of duty had been enhanced and that police salaries were also being increased. Asked about the non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, Mr Kundi said Mr Afridi was in safe hands, adding that nobody could predict what would happen in the future. The governor’s adviser on information, Samar Haroon Bilour, said the police and Counter-Terrorism Department needed modern weapons, secure vehicles, tracking systems and protective equipment to improve their operational capacity. She said sustained federal support was necessary to strengthen both institutions. Earlier in the day, DSP Imranuddin and Constable Jan, who were martyred during an operation against terrorists in Karak district on Thursday, were laid to rest in their native villages in Charsadda with police honours. Mr Kundi claimed that weapons left behind following the withdrawal of international forces from Afghanistan had fallen into the hands of terrorists. He said Pakistan’s long border with Afghanistan made surveillance difficult in some areas and that terrorists possessed sophisticated weapons. Federal package Separately, addressing a news conference at Governor House in Peshawar, Mr Kundi said demands presented by the provincial advisory council at the Apex Committee meeting on Thursday had been accepted by PM Shehbaz. “Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a package of Rs160 billion for the province. To resolve issues related to gas and wheat, the prime minister directed the secretary of food department to convene a meeting soon,” he said. According to the governor, the meeting, attended by the prime minister and senior military leadership, focused on security, development and public concerns in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Mr Kundi said peace was essential for development and investment in the province. “If there is peace in the province, there will be development and investment will also come from abroad,” he said. He added that the provincial advisory council would pursue KP’s rights on the basis of facts and said talks had also been held with representatives of the Awami National Party, Jamaat-i-Islami and Qaumi Watan Party chief Aftab Ahmad Khan Sherpao. Mr Kundi said political parties needed to unite over the province’s rights. He also raised the issue of KP’s water share, insisting that the province was not receiving its due allocation under the 1991 water accord. He said the federal government had heard the province’s position and tenders for packages one and four of the Chashma Lift Canal would be issued next month. Ms Bilour said development priorities discussed with the federal government included road connectivity, educational institutions, information technology hubs and vocational training facilities. She said improving security and providing young people with better educational and employment opportunities were both necessary for the province’s long-term development. Mr Kundi said restoring peace, strengthening the police and securing the province’s constitutional and development rights were essential for KP’s future. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026
