items.title: Return of Ebola: Triumph of 2014, test of 2026
items.description: By Sola Ogundipe October 20 has acquired an unsettling significance in Nigeria’s public health history. 12 years ago, on that date, the World Health Organisation (WHO) declared Nigeria free of Ebola after a painstaking campaign halted an outbreak that threatened to overwhelm the country’s fragile health system. On October 20, 2026, the confirmation of an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja reopened an uncomfortable question: how prepared is Nigeria to confront the virus again? The coincidence is striking, but the lesson is more important than the date. The 2014 victory demonstrated what decisive leadership, vigilant surveillance, contact tracing and coordinated action could achieve. The new case tests whether those hard won lessons have translated into lasting capacity. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare confirmed the case on October 20 following laboratory testing. He said the patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, reportedly developed symptoms on October 7, sought care at a private health facility in Abuja on October 11 and tested positive on October 20. She was isolated and receiving medical care, while investigations continued to establish the likely source of infection and reconstruct her travel and exposure history. The ministry reported that 44 contacts had been identified for monitoring. The warning hidden in a victory Nigeria’s 2014 experience remains one of Africa’s most cited examples of successful Ebola containment. The outbreak began after Liberian-American Patrick Sawyer arrived in Lagos in July 2014 while infected with the virus. His illness exposed health workers and others to a disease that many facilities had limited experience managing. Nigeria recorded 20 cases, including eight deaths, before the outbreak was contained. The response required the identification and monitoring of hundreds of contacts, the isolation of suspected cases, rapid investigation and sustained public communication. On October 20, 2014, the World Health Organisation (WHO) formally declared Nigeria Ebola-free after 42 days without a new case following the discharge of the last confirmed patient. Dr Rui Gama Vaz, then WHO representative in Nigeria, captured the significance of the achievement while warning against complacency. “It shows that Ebola can be contained, but we must be clear that we have only won a battle, the war will only end when West Africa and other affected countries are also declared free of Ebola,” he said at the declaration ceremony. His words have acquired fresh relevance. Nigeria won that battle through a combination of epidemiological investigation, disciplined contact tracing, isolation, laboratory support and cooperation between public authorities and private institutions. The achievement was not simply a declaration. It was the result of work carried out by public health teams, clinicians, laboratory personnel and communities under considerable pressure. But victories in public health can breed a dangerous illusion: that because a country defeats a threat once, it will necessarily defeat it again. Ebola has returned in a different form, under different circumstances and against a public health system facing its own constraints. The anniversary should therefore be less a celebration of past success than an examination of what has endured since 2014. New strain, different challenges The virus responsible for the Abuja case is Bundibugyo, a species of Ebola virus distinct from the Zaire ebolavirus associated with the 2014 Nigerian outbreak. That distinction is clinically important because vaccines and treatments developed for one Ebola species cannot automatically be assumed to work against another. According to WHO, there is currently no approved vaccine or specific antiviral treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola, but that does not mean the disease is untreatable. Prompt diagnosis, isolation, careful supportive care and management of complications can be critical to a patient’s survival and to preventing further transmission. Professor Oyewale Tomori, virologist and chairman of the West African National Academy of Scientists, has warned against treating the strain’s comparatively lower historical fatality rates as grounds for complacency. “When we say Bundibugyo is less severe, however, that does not mean it is harmless or that it cannot kill people,” he said. The distinction also exposes a potential weakness in preparedness. Equipment, diagnostic protocols and clinical experience acquired during an earlier outbreak cannot simply be assumed to provide everything required for a different strain. Diagnosis gap One of the most consequential questions concerns the interval between the patient’s first symptoms and laboratory confirmation. The reported timeline places the onset of symptoms on October 7, the first medical consultation on October 11 and laboratory confirmation on October 20. Tomori has questioned whether the diagnosis could have been made sooner, particularly given the patient’s travel history and the outbreak already under way elsewhere in Africa. “We need to improve on that,” he said, referring to the time taken to confirm the case. His concern goes to the heart of outbreak control. Early Ebola symptoms can resemble common illnesses, including malaria. But when a patient has recently travelled from a region affected by an outbreak, that history must change the clinical assessment. The 44 contacts identified by the Federal Ministry of Health represent an important starting point, not the end of the investigation. Nigeria’s 2014 response showed the value of rapidly identifying contacts and following them systematically. The present outbreak demands the same discipline, supported by reliable data and a clear chain of command. No fragmented responses The Abuja case is part of a wider regional emergency. The Bundibugyo outbreak was declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, and infections have subsequently been detected in other countries, including Kenya. On October 20, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Director-General Dr Jean Kaseya called for urgent international support following Nigeria’s confirmation. He described the outbreak as the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history and appealed for financing, medical supplies, diagnostics, trained responders and stronger community surveillance. “My appeal to the international community is urgent: act now,” Kaseya said. His appeal reflects a basic reality of epidemic control: viruses do not respect national borders, and no country can manage a cross-border outbreak effectively in isolation. The WHO has called for sustained readiness across the region, including laboratory capacity, rapid-response teams, infection prevention measures, essential supplies and community engagement. It has also advised against restrictions on travel or trade with affected countries. For Nigeria, the challenge is to translate these recommendations into dependable systems that function outside emergency press briefings. What October 20 should now mean Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola victory remains a defining moment. It showed what swift action, sound coordination and the courage of health workers and communities could achieve in the face of a deadly outbreak. But winning that battle then is no guarantee of winning the next one. The coincidence of October 20, 12 years apart, brings that lesson into sharp focus. “Preparedness cannot be switched on when an outbreak strikes and forgotten when it passes.” Surveillance must continue, laboratories must be ready to investigate unusual infections, and health workers need regular training. Private hospitals and clinics, often the first point of contact for sick patients, must also be part of the national response. Essential supplies, isolation facilities and reliable communication systems must be in place before they’re needed. On October 20, 2014, Nigeria celebrated a hard won victory. On the same date in 2026, it was reminded that such victories are never permanent. The date has come full circle, but the outcome isn’t predetermined. Whether this episode becomes another story of successful containment or exposes the cost of neglected preparedness will depend on the decisions Nigeria makes no Prevention tips: What you should do 1. Avoid contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of anyone who is ill with suspected Ebola. 2. Do not touch the body or bodily fluids of someone who has died from suspected Ebola 3. Wash hands regularly with soap and water. 4. Seek urgent medical assessment if symptoms develop after a possible exposure, and call ahead so the facility can prepare for safe assessment 5. Follow instructions from public health authorities if identified as a contact Vanguard News The post Return of Ebola: Triumph of 2014, test of 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ECP proposes AI rules for parties, media, election observers
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has proposed amendments to the codes of conduct for political parties and contesting candidates, media and election observers to protect the electoral process from the harmful effects of artificial intelligence (AI). The commission has shared the draft amendments with stakeholders and sought their feedback by Nov 20. According to a draft notification issued on Friday, the ECP cited its constitutional duty under Article 218(3) to ensure honest, just and fair elections. “Therefore, it is the core responsibility of the commission to take all necessary steps to guard against corrupt practices, which also include manipulation of the electoral process through misleading content generated using AI,” the notification said. Draft bars digitally manipulated ‘defamatory content’; feedback sought by Nov 20 Under the proposed rules, political parties and contesting candidates would be required to clearly disclose all AI-generated campaign material, including deepfake images, audio, video and synthetic voices. Robocalls and voter outreach messages using cloned voices would have to disclose their AI-generated nature at the outset. The draft prohibits AI-generated content intended to deceive voters or misrepresent individuals. It also bans false, derogatory or defamatory deepfake statements targeting candidates, party leaders, supporters, election officials, the judiciary, state functionaries or the armed forces. Political parties would be barred from using automated bots or acco­unts to artificially inflate likes, comments, shares or followers to create a false impression of public support. They would also be required to retain logs of all AI-assisted campaign content and submit them to the ECP upon request. Print, electronic and digital media outlets, as well as social media influencers, would be required to explicitly label AI-altered election content. Media houses would remain legally responsible for the factual accuracy of content produced using AI tools for translation, anchoring or analysis. The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency will actively monitor online platforms. They will submit compliance reports to the ECP, which retains the authority to order immediate content takedowns or re-labelling. Election observers would be required to identify and promptly report AI-generated deepfakes and disinformation campaigns directly to the ECP without further spreading the misleading material. They would also be prohibited from using AI to fabricate or embellish election photographs, videos, reports or field observations. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: EES, ETIAS and €20 Fee: How confusion over Europe’s new border systems fuels visa scam
items.description: By Vera Anyagafu A new digital stamp at Europe’s airports is free. The €20 travel authorisation some Nigerians are talking about does not apply to Nigerian visa applicants to Europe. Yet from Instagram vendors in Surulere to travel plazas in Onitsha, agents are charging Nigerian travellers up to N250,000 for both. Since 10 April 2026, every Nigerian arriving in Paris or Frankfurt on a short-stay Schengen visa no longer gets an ink stamp. A camera and fingerprint scanner logs you into Europe’s Entry/Exit System (EES) automatically, at no cost. The other system, the European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS), is the source of the rumour. It will eventually cost €20, valid for three years, but it is only for travellers who do not need a visa to enter Europe, like Americans, British, Australians and Canadians. For Nigerians, who still need a Schengen visa, ETIAS is never required. If someone in Nigeria is charging you for it, you are paying for something you do not need. That gap is where the exploitation happens. The EES became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all 29 Schengen countries. You do not apply for it in advance. When you land in Paris or Frankfurt, you look at a camera, place your fingers on a scanner, and your entry is recorded digitally, replacing the old ink stamp. It applies to all non-European nationals on short stays, which includes every Nigerian travelling on a Schengen visa, and it automatically calculates your period of stay. ETIAS is different. It is a pre-travel check only for visa-exempt travellers, people who do not need a Schengen visa to visit Europe. For Nigerians who need a visa, ETIAS is never required. If you need a Schengen visa today, you will continue to use the visa process through VFS Global or TLSContact in Lagos and Abuja. The official fee for ETIAS, when it eventually launches, will be €20 for travellers aged 18 to 70, free for under 18 and over 70, and any additional charges will go to commercial intermediaries. The only official website where the application will be available once launched is the European Union’s official ETIAS portal, and the information portal for both systems is the official Travel Europe portal managed by the European Union. And for travellers who will eventually need it, the system is not yet open. The official portal has made it clear that no action is required at this time, and any website currently offering to process an application is not legitimate. HOW THE SCAM WORKS Consular Hub gathered that the European authorities have already identified over a hundred unofficial websites providing information on ETIAS. These sites use convincing designs and domain names to mimic legitimate portals. Since the programme is on hold, any site requesting a €20 fee today is considered fraudulent. Travellers are warned to be very cautious because it is not currently possible to apply for an official ETIAS authorisation since the system is not operational yet. Many of these third-party sites charge inflated fees or steal personal information. In Nigeria the pattern is now familiar. Take Sola, a 28-year-old applicant in Surulere. A travel agent on Instagram operating as Travel with Tayo told her she needed to pay N65,000 naira for mandatory ETIAS registration before her Schengen visa appointment at VFS Global. She paid and was given a receipt that looked official with a European Union logo. At her appointment, VFS Global told her ETIAS does not apply to Nigerians and the paper was worthless. Or Emeka, a trader in Onitsha who wanted to visit his brother in Milan. An agent in his local plaza operating as Blessed Travels collected tens of thousands of naira, for EES biometric pre-registration and ETIAS approval, promising fast-track entry. He arrived in Rome to find his entry under EES was recorded fresh at the border anyway and the extra papers meant nothing. TO STAY SAFE To stay safe as a Nigerian passport holder, remember three things; You do not pay €20 for ETIAS, you pay about €90 for the Schengen visa itself at VFS Global or TLSContact. The Entry/Exit System costs nothing and you do not pre-register for it. And only use the official portals for information, as the protection of your personal data cannot be guaranteed if you use another website. Vanguard News The post EES, ETIAS and €20 Fee: How confusion over Europe’s new border systems fuels visa scam appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at training
items.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club’s second team train on Friday. The 40-year-old had been unwell with a virus and missed the pre-match news conference on Tuesday prior to Bayern’s Champions League game against Arsenal. The former Manchester City and Belgium defender was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday. Reports in Germany say Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital. “Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during an FC Bayern reserve team training session on Friday,” said a statement from the Bundesliga club., external “The first-team head coach was watching the second string’s session. “Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical care. “His coaching staff will oversee training and match activities until further notice.” Bayern’s next game is against Freiburg in the German top flight on Sunday. “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure his speedy recovery,” said Bayern sporting director Max Eberl. “Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs. “His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.” Aaron Danks, one of Kompany’s assistants, took the pre-match news conference for Bayern before the Arsenal game. German football journalist Taufig Khalil told BBC Radio 5 Live that Kompany had been “suffering with the virus for about a week”. He added: “The thing started last weekend on Saturday against Leipzig, and that’s the first time we saw Vincent Kompany [when] he didn’t look very well. “He didn’t do the press conference after, and Max Eberl told us that he’s suffering with a virus. “Everybody was really surprised that Vincent Kompany was standing there with his black jacket in the pouring rain of Munich on Wednesday night against Arsenal. Everybody expected Aaron Danks to be there. “The problem was that maybe you couldn’t bench Vincent Kompany, the game was too important for him. “Bayern Munich just told us that he’s in stable conditions. There was a helicopter involved in the whole thing, which landed on the training ground at Bayern Munich, but he was not brought into the hospital by helicopter. They brought him with a medical car and he will be now there.” ‘Get well soon, Vinny’ Kompany left his role as Burnley manager to take over at Bayern in May 2024, succeeding current England manager Thomas Tuchel. He had won the Championship with Burnley in 2022-23 and, despite the Clarets being relegated from the Premier League under him the following season, Kompany was appointed by the Bundesliga club. He has led Bayern to the German top-flight title in the past two seasons and reached the 2025-26 Champions League semi-finals before being beaten by eventual winners Paris St-Germain. Kompany spent 11 years at Manchester City as a player, winning four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and four League Cups. “Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and club legend, Vincent Kompany,” said City in a post on social media. “Get well soon, Vinny.” “Everyone here at Burnley FC sends our best wishes to Vincent and we wish him a speedy recovery,” said a Burnley statement.

items.title: A Very Suspicious Indictment of Two Former FBI Officials
items.description: Not too long ago, the Department of Justice could generally be trusted to prosecute cases in which lawyers believed that real wrongdoing had occurred. Now DOJ frequently unveils lawsuits that seem designed mostly for securing likes and reposts on right-wing social media—the actual facts be damned. Any high-profile criminal case brought by the Trump administration arrives with an air of suspicion. Today, Jeanine Pirro, the top federal prosecutor for Washington, D.C., announced an odd set of charges against two former FBI officials for allegedly lying to Congress during testimony in 2023. “When senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” Pirro posted on X. For all of the fanfare, DOJ provided little evidence to back up its claims. But the timing of the charges—they’ve arrived just more than a week before the midterm elections—and with the puzzling substance of the allegations and the administration’s crowing online, does not inspire confidence in the integrity of the prosecutorial work. The charges concern several statements made by the defendants, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, in the course of a congressional investigation into supposed “weaponization” of the government against President Trump. In brief, the Justice Department is alleging that Floris and Benavides lied to the House Judiciary Committee regarding their level of knowledge about the FBI’s handling of Hunter Biden’s laptop. Lawyers for Floris issued a statement saying that DOJ “has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts.” Benavides’s lawyer likewise described the charges as “baseless.” The saga of the Hunter Biden laptop has now spanned four federal elections, and the specifics of the story may, reasonably, no longer be top of mind. Understanding its relevance here requires a deep plunge into far-right mythology. But the quick version is that MAGA became obsessed with the possibly stolen laptop, and the material it contained documenting Biden’s drug addiction, after the New York Post published an article about the laptop in the lead-up to the 2020 election. Social-media companies, burned by their experience of Russian election interference in 2016, worried that the underlying documents might be Russian misinformation. (This suspicion was never confirmed.) They responded aggressively by suppressing links to the Post ’s story—which outraged the right. The laptop would go on to play a starring role in the coming years as the GOP used congressional investigations to tell a story about the victimization of the right, supposedly having been a target of a sprawling network of government-backed online censorship and unfair treatment by the FBI. This was the context in which Floris and Benavides were testifying in 2023. The two had held leadership positions in the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF) during 2020, a section created to respond to foreign interference after Russia’s 2016 election meddling. There they had crossed paths with the laptop. In recent years, congressional Republicans have pointed to various decontextualized snippets of that testimony and internal FBI documents as part of their efforts to suggest that the FBI was working against Trump in the 2020 election. By then, for a certain kind of very online Trump supporter, Floris and Benavides had already become familiar if relatively minor villains in the anticanon of deep-state enemies. The criminal charges today make sense in this larger narrative. In his X post announcing the charges, FBI Director Kash Patel referred to the agency’s past “political weaponization targeting their opponents.” Just because MAGA hates someone does not mean that they are innocent. But Floris and Benavides’s work as described in the affidavit seems unremarkable. And the document is opaque when describing what the two defendants are actually alleged to have lied about. To be prosecutable under the relevant statute, a lie to government authorities must be told “knowingly and willfully,” and it must be “material” in a way that substantively affects the investigation in question. Some of Floris’s and Benavides’s alleged misstatements, as described in the affidavit, don’t initially appear to be misstatements at all. For example, Floris said she was not involved in the criminal investigation into Hunter Biden during which the FBI seized the laptop; in fact, her work at the FITF really was separate from the criminal probe, which was carried out by a different team. Other supposed lies might well be better understood as forgetfulness. The two defendants were high up in the bureau and wouldn’t necessarily recall the minutiae of an incident that took place three years before they testified. In one instance, the affidavit alleges that Floris lied about her involvement in “an assessment to discredit the Hunter Biden investigations,” but contains no further mention of this supposed assessment nor any quotes from the relevant testimony. Perhaps DOJ will be able to provide more evidence for its allegations as the case goes on, but as things now stand, the charges appear less than airtight. How the Justice Department chose to bring this case also invites suspicion. The charges were filed via a criminal complaint, a method the government uses in many investigations that must move quickly, because a complaint does not require the immediate involvement of a grand jury. The need to rush here is hard to see, given that the relevant testimony was three years ago. Conversely, it’s easy to imagine why DOJ would want to push out incendiary allegations without having to convince a potentially skeptical grand jury—an all-but-certainty in D.C., where jurors have delivered a number of high-profile rebuttals to federal prosecutors. In the next 30 days, if the department wishes to move forward with the case, it will have to seek a grand jury’s indictment. By then, though, the Trump administration may have already gotten the propaganda boost it was looking for. At a hearing today, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui appeared skeptical of the case, noting the government’s decision to delay seeking an indictment and describing the defendants’ “sparkling backgrounds.” As many judges have commented over the past year, the traditional “presumption of regularity” awarded to the Justice Department’s work has been eroded by the Trump administration’s habitual use of criminal prosecutions as a tool to harass the president’s enemies. With this case, DOJ has provided little material to reassure its critics.

items.title: Netanyahu says Israel is planning a major West Bank military operation
items.description: Israel is preparing a major military operation in the West Bank, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday, as local sources reported that Israeli forces had demolished a residential building in Hebron and closed the city's main entrances following a shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian attackers. The Israel Defense Forces said it had launched raids in Hebron and nearby villages following the attack, in which three other Israeli soldiers were slightly wounded. The military said it was investigating, together with the Shin Bet domestic security agency, whether the attackers belonged to an isolated cell or were linked to a larger militant cell. Speaking in Hebron, Netanyahu said the military would apply the operational model it had used in refugee camps to neighborhoods from which the attackers had emerged. Netanyahu said that under the plan, residents would be evacuated, troops would conduct house-to-house searches, weapons would be seized and what he called "terrorist infrastructure" would be destroyed. Netanyahu added that he and the defense minister had reviewed plans for a large-scale military operation in the West Bank, describing it as an operation unlike any carried out since the 1967 Middle East war. He said the military was ready to carry it out, but that the timing had yet to be decided. In response, the Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates condemned Israel's tightening of restrictions in Hebron, warning that the measures could lead to further violence and collective punishment. Palestinian sources said Israeli forces demolished a building containing three apartments in the Farsh al-Hawa area west of Hebron, each covering about 200 square meters. Israel also tightened restrictions at entrances and exits to cities across the West Bank and closed many checkpoints and iron gates in the southern, central and northern areas, according to Palestinian security sources. Local sources said Israeli forces closed Hebron and its main entrances. Roads linking the city to nearby areas were also closed. Hebron is a major economic center in the West Bank. The closure of its entrances has disrupted daily life in the area, which is home to more than one million Palestinians, according to Israeli reports. (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: Santé mentale au Maroc : 6,5 millions de personnes concernées, 85 % sans prise en charge adaptée
items.description: Près de 6,5 millions de Marocains souffriraient de troubles psychiques, dont environ deux millions d’enfants et de jeunes adolescents. Selon les données de la Coalition professionnelle des psychologues cliniciens du Maroc, près de 85 % des personnes concernées ne bénéficieraient pas de soins appropriés. Face à ces besoins, les professionnels appellent à renforcer la prévention, élargir l’accès aux traitements et accélérer la mise en œuvre du plan national de santé mentale à l’horizon 2030. La santé mentale représente un enjeu majeur de santé publique au Maroc. Selon des données relayées par la Coalition professionnelle des psychologues cliniciens du Maroc, près de 6,5 millions de personnes seraient concernées par des troubles psychiques dans le Royaume. Parmi elles, environ deux millions seraient des enfants et de jeunes adolescents. Plus préoccupant encore, près de 85 % des personnes concernées ne recevraient pas de prise en charge adaptée. Ces chiffres mettent en lumière le décalage entre les besoins de la population et les moyens disponibles pour y répondre. Pour les patients et leurs familles, les difficultés peuvent se traduire par un accès limité aux spécialistes, des délais d’attente, des dépenses importantes et des parcours de soins interrompus. L’absence de prise en charge précoce peut également favoriser l’isolement et aggraver les difficultés rencontrées. Prévention et accès aux soins : des priorités Face à cette situation, la Coalition professionnelle des psychologues cliniciens du Maroc plaide pour un renforcement des actions de prévention et du dépistage précoce. Elle appelle également à faciliter l’accès aux consultations psychologiques et psychiatriques, ainsi qu’à développer des structures de proximité. L’amélioration du remboursement des soins figure aussi parmi les priorités avancées par les professionnels. Le coût des consultations et des traitements peut en effet constituer un frein pour les ménages, notamment lorsque l’accompagnement nécessite un suivi régulier sur une longue période. Les spécialistes demandent par ailleurs une modernisation du cadre juridique encadrant l’exercice de la psychologie clinique, un renforcement de la formation continue et une augmentation des ressources humaines spécialisées. La prise en charge des jeunes constitue un enjeu spécifique. Les troubles psychiques peuvent se manifester à l’école, au sein de la famille ou dans les structures sociales. Une meilleure coordination entre les secteurs de la santé, de l’éducation et de l’action sociale permettrait de repérer plus tôt les difficultés et d’orienter les personnes concernées vers des professionnels compétents. Sans passerelles efficaces entre ces différents acteurs, les signes de souffrance psychologique risquent de ne pas être identifiés à temps, retardant ainsi l’accès à un accompagnement adapté. Un plan national doté d’un budget prévisionnel de près de 4 milliards de dirhams Le plan national de santé mentale à l’horizon 2030 prévoit une enveloppe budgétaire proche de 4 milliards de dirhams. L’enjeu sera de traduire les moyens annoncés en améliorations concrètes pour les patients : recrutement de professionnels, ouverture de structures, meilleure couverture territoriale et remboursement effectif des soins. L’évaluation de ce plan devra également s’appuyer sur des indicateurs mesurables, notamment l’évolution du taux de prise en charge, la disponibilité des spécialistes dans les différentes régions et la réduction des délais d’accès aux consultations. Au-delà des moyens financiers et humains, la lutte contre les préjugés liés aux troubles psychiques demeure essentielle. La peur du jugement et la stigmatisation peuvent dissuader certaines personnes de demander de l’aide ou les conduire à retarder leur consultation. Les médias, les universités, les associations et les professionnels de santé ont un rôle à jouer pour mieux informer le public et encourager le recours aux soins psychologiques et psychiatriques. L’enjeu ne se limite donc pas au financement d’un plan national. Il consiste aussi à garantir que les personnes concernées, notamment les enfants, les adolescents et les ménages les plus vulnérables, puissent accéder à un accompagnement adapté, accessible et continu. The post Santé mentale au Maroc : 6,5 millions de personnes concernées, 85 % sans prise en charge adaptée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sénégal Le Premier ministre sénégalais répond à l’invitation au débat d’Ousmane Sonko.
items.description: Le Premier ministre sénégalais, Al Aminou Lô, a réagi à l’invitation d’Ousmane Sonko à un débat public sur le budget. Il a rappelé les priorités des Sénégalais, notamment la vie chère. « Voilà les attentes des Sénégalais, qui ne se résolvent ni par des discours et blocages institutionnels, ni par des luttes syndicales déconnectées des réalités du Sénégal profond », a-t-il déclaré. Al Aminou Lô a expliqué qu’il préférait se concentrer sur les urgences du pays. « En ma qualité de chef du gouvernement, mon temps et mes forces intellectuelles et physiques sont mobilisés sur ces urgences, plutôt que sur des débats qui ne disposent d’une seule enceinte institutionnelle : le Parlement », a-t-il affirmé. Le désaccord porte sur la loi de finances rectificative de 2026. Ousmane Sonko critique notamment les choix du gouvernement concernant les subventions aux produits pétroliers et les aides sociales. items.title: Cuban FM denounces Trump's new military threat
items.description: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez on Friday denounced a new threat of military intervention against the Caribbean nation by US President Donald Trump. In a post on X, Rodriguez rejected "any threat regarding US ambitions toward Cuba" in response to remarks by Trump, who said Friday that US ships "will pass" Cuba on their way back from Iran. "They'll raise up their hands. And then we're going to send (Secretary of State) Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," Trump said at a campaign rally in Fort Myers, in the southern US state of Florida. He said one of the ships would stop about 50 yards (about 46 meters) off the coast. "On our shores there are beautiful beaches, but also diente de perro (a jagged coastal coral formation), inhospitable to those who arrive with hostile aims and a thirst for domination," Rodriguez wrote. Rodriguez, Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel and other officials have denounced US threats of military intervention, which have escalated since early 2026, and defended the island's sovereignty and its right to self-defense. In May, Trump said in Florida that the United States would be taking over Cuba "almost immediately."

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire : A’Salfo en deuil, son frère jumeau Issouf est décédé en France.
items.description: Le chanteur ivoirien A'Salfo, de son vrai nom Salif Traoré, traverse une douloureuse épreuve. Le leader du groupe Magic System a annoncé le décès de son frère jumeau, Issouf Traoré, survenu le mercredi 21 octobre 2026 en France des suites d'une maladie. « Je suis désormais seul » C'est sur sa page Facebook, dans un message empreint d'une profonde émotion, que l'artiste a annoncé la triste nouvelle. Il y confie avoir veillé son frère jusqu'à son dernier souffle. « Tu as demandé que je sois à tes côtés pour les dernières secondes de ta vie, comme à nos premières minutes dans ce monde », a-t-il écrit, avant de conclure : « Je suis désormais seul. Repose en paix, Issouf. » Les deux jumeaux étaient liés par une relation que l'on devine fusionnelle. Les mots d'A'Salfo des « premières minutes dans ce monde » aux « dernières secondes » de la vie de son frère traduisent toute la force de ce lien unissant deux êtres nés le même jour et accompagnés l'un l'autre jusque dans l'épreuve. Figure emblématique de la musique ivoirienne et africaine, A'Salfo incarne, avec Magic System, la joie et la ferveur populaire depuis des décennies. Son deuil personnel dépasse donc largement le cercle familial, tant le chanteur et son groupe occupent une place à part dans le cœur des Ivoiriens et des mélomanes du continent. Les messages de soutien et les hommages devraient affluer dans les prochaines heures, à la mesure de l'affection que le public porte à l'artiste. La rédaction du journal L'Œil du Sahara a dresse ses sincères condoléances à A'Salfo, à sa famille et à ses proches. En ces moments de douleur, nos pensées les accompagnent. items.title: Gov AbdulRazaq inaugurates PBAT Door-to-Door campaign in Kwara
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq on Monday inaugurated the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT) Door-to-Door Movement in Ilorin, the state capital, signalling the commencement of campaigns for the re-election of President Tinubu in the state. Performing the inauguration of the group’s executives, the governor tasked them to work hard in their mobilization campaigns and convey the impacts of the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu to all the nooks and crannies of the state. He commended the leadership of the movement for establishing a platform to communicate the life-changing policies and programmes of the Federal Government to the people. He also charged the members to listen to the concerns of the people, provide feedback to the government and communicate its programmes effectively. AbdulRazaq further urged them to obtain accurate information about government programmes through official channels and share it with residents, while emphasising the need for peaceful and respectful engagement. “The movement must not only take government messages to the people but also bring their concerns back to the relevant authorities to guide policy adjustments and improve living standards,” the governor stressed, advising them to shun violence in the course of their engagements. He also called for cooperation between the movement and all APC structures from the National leadership to ward’s officials and polling unit committees, saying they are all working for a common goal. He added that this initiative must be sustained beyond the inauguration ceremony and its activities should translate into continuous grassroots engagement rather than a one-off event. Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly and APC gubernatorial candidate, Rt Hon Salihu Yakubu Danladi, expressed confidence that Kwarans will vote massively for APC, following Governor AbdulRazaq’s achievements which are visible across 193 wards of the state. He said the governor has performed exceedingly well in various sectors including infrastructural development, civil service, pension administration, and the welfare of youths, women and senior citizens among others. According to him, “APC has sufficient achievements to campaign on and does not need to resort to insulting political opponents. Tinubu is for Kwara, and Kwara is for Tinubu. By God’s grace, 2027 is for the APC. We know where we are today, and we are moving forward”. Kwara state APC Chairman, Prince Sunday Fagbemi, in his remark said the party hass prospects ahead of the 2027 general elections, noting that the APC is determined to win all elective positions in the state. Fagbemi said the party remained committed to securing victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the governorship candidate, and all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats. He dismissed claims of alternative political arrangements in Kwara, maintaining that the party’s position had been reinforced by statements from President Tinubu and the Minister of FCT, while warning opposition groups against relying on financial inducements to challenge the APC. The APC Chairman maintained that the party would retain its political strength in Kwara and return victorious in the 2027 elections. Founder and Grand Patron of the Movement, High Chief Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo (a.k.a Tompolo), in his address urged the people of the State to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Represented by High Chief Kestin Pondi, Ekpemupolo urged Nigerians not to be misled by political opponents, stressing that sustained support for Tinubu will help improve security, infrastructure, healthcare and education. Ekpemupolo then announced a donation of 34 campaign vehicles to the Movement in a bid to aid their mobility across the state, as part of the group’s grassroots mobilisation strategy. National Coordinator of PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Comrade Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, urged the people of Kwara to give President Tinubu massive support ìn the upcoming polls. Asuku, who commended Governor AbdulRazaq’s records of service in the state and his continued support for the President, said the governor is doing greatly for Kwara because of the president’s backing. items.title: Kwara govt distributes farm inputs to 235,567 farmers
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin Kwara State Governor, Mallam AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq last Monday commenced distribution of agricultural inputs, productive assets and processing equipment to 49,337 local farmers and vulnerable households in the state. 186, 230 residents had earlier benefitted from the initiative which brings the total beneficiaries to 235,567. The initiative is being carried out under FADAMA CARES 2.0 which is supported by Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES). While performing the flag-off in Ilorin, Governor AbdulRazaq said farmers were facing some challenges and therefore needed regular support to reduce their losses and earn more. His words: “Our farmers are facing some challenges which include costly inputs, unpredictable weather, limited equipment and the difficulties of moving and processing their produce. Our duty is to remove these barriers and obstacles so that they will not labor in vain. “This programme has reached 186,230 beneficiaries. Of this, 54,332 received inputs and services while 131,898 received productive and processing assets across 10 value chains. These beneficiaries are farmers, processors, and families earning better livelihood. This latest programme will support 49,337 beneficiaries. It provides rice, maize, soybeans inputs. It also provides equipment ranging from sprayers, water pumps, and power tillers to rice mills. “We also have cassava processors, fish smoking plants, and commercial boats. This programme will reach a total of 235,556 beneficiaries. Our goal is to help farmers produce more, lose less, process better, reach wider markets and earn more with opportunities for women and young people.” He congratulated the beneficiaries and enjoined them to see the inputs and assets as investment opportunities and not as handouts. The governor also acknowledged the active roles played by different stakeholders to make the programme a huge success. Commissioner for Livestock who is supervising the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, Hon Olohuntoyosi Thomas, in her address at the event said the government has deployed 48 tractors and two D&R caterpillar bulldozers to drive farming activities and expand agricultural mechanization across the 16 local governments. Thomas said 2,016 state farmers were provided with 8,064 bags of NPK fertilizer through the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Farm Input Support Programme. She appreciated all key stakeholders whose contributions have developed the sector, including development partners, public-private investors, farmers’ associations, and traditional institutions. Similarly, Commissioner for Finance and Chairman State NG-CARES Steering Committee, Dr Hauwa Nuru, said Kwara was one of the leading states in delivery and reimbursement, adding that the initiative reflects the commitment of the administration in empowering farmers, improving their livelihoods, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable economic growth. State Project Coordinator, FADAMA NG-CARES, Dr Busari Toyin Isiaka, in his remark explained that FADAMA CARES 2.0 is the agricultural component of NG-CARES, supported by the World Bank through additional financing, adding that its purpose was to improve agricultural production, reduce losses, enhance food security and strengthen beneficiaries’ incomes. Busari listed items for distribution as rice, maize and soybean inputs, adding that relevant production inputs such as knapsack sprayers, water pumps, power tillers, grinding machines, rice mills, cassava processing equipment, fish smoking kilns and commercial boats would also be distributed. State Chairman for the Federated FADAMA Community Association (FFCA), Alhaji Isiaka Yakub Falala, appreciated Governor AbdulRazaq for the administration’s commitment in turning around the agricultural sector and his support for farmers in the state. items.title: Causes et conséquences des manifestations de masse en France : Crise systémique de l’éducation et perspectives politiques
items.description: Oleg Nesterenko, Président du CCIE (www.c-cie.eu) Transcription de l’interview avec le média russe « Politnavigator » Politnavigator : Quelles sont les causes des manifestations de masse en France ? Oleg Nesterenko : Les manifestations massives d'écoliers et d'étudiants qui ont secoué la France depuis septembre, et se sont intensifiées en octobre 2026, trouvent leur origine dans des années de crise systémique au sein du système éducatif français. Le catalyseur immédiat de ces événements a été le projet de budget de l’État pour 2027. Contrairement aux assurances du gouvernement, qui prévoient une augmentation du budget de l'éducation de 1,1 à 1,2 milliard d'euros par rapport à 2026, la réalité est loin des déclarations optimistes du groupement politique dirigé par Emmanuel Macron. La France est confrontée à une grave pénurie d'enseignants, dont la formation est souvent insuffisante, ainsi que de personnel scolaire. Cette pénurie de personnel enseignant et non-enseignant, conjuguée à des salles de classe surpeuplées et à une prolongation de la journée scolaire, atteignant parfois 14 heures, témoigne des efforts désespérés pour pallier le manque de moyens. De plus, la grande majorité des établissements scolaires publics se situent dans un état de délabrement avancé et parfois d'urgence des infrastructures. Un autre facteur de profond mécontentement chez les jeunes réside dans l'incertitude de l'avenir, particulièrement lors de l'entrée dans l'enseignement supérieur. Le processus d'admission, fortement dépendant du système Parcoursup , est largement critiqué pour son manque de transparence et son inefficacité, apportant beaucoup plus d’inconvénients que d’avantages. Politnavigator : Comment cela affecte-t-il la position de Macron ? Oleg Nesterenko : Il convient de noter qu’au moment de l’élection d’Emmanuel Macron à la présidence en 2017, son taux d’approbation s’élevait à environ 45 %. Au début de sa politique hostile envers la Russie en 2022, ce chiffre était tombé à 36 %, pour atteindre aujourd’hui à peine 15 %. Après son prédécesseur et bienfaiteur, François Hollande, qu’Emmanuel Macron a brutalement trahi en 2017, il est devenu le dirigeant français le moins populaire de l’histoire de la Ve République, fondée en 1958, soit depuis près de 70 ans. Pour une majorité de citoyens français, il incarne une source d’agacement, voire de haine. Politnavigator : Cette impopularité aura-t-elle un impact sur les résultats des prochaines élections présidentielles ? Oleg Nesterenko : Indubitablement, elle influencera le scrutin prévu pour avril 2027. Il convient de noter qu’Emmanuel Macron, ayant terminé son deuxième mandat présidentiel, n’est pas rééligible. Sa carrière politique en France est terminée. La politique anti-russe menée ces dernières années, devenue une caractéristique de son règne, est étroitement liée à ses rêves de longue date de succéder à Ursula von der Leyen au poste de « Gauleiter » de la Commission européenne. Deux potentiels successeurs d’Emmanuel Macron, les anciens Premiers ministres Édouard Philippe et Gabriel Attal, devraient se présenter aux prochaines élections. Étant donné que ces individus représentent une continuité directe de la politique destructrice de Macron, les événements qui se multiplient dans les rues françaises affecteront inévitablement leurs perspectives électorales. Politnavigator : Comment les événements actuels affecteront-ils la politique étrangère française sur la Russie et l’Ukraine ? Oleg Nesterenko : Malgré la résurgence de chants russes en langue française de l’époque de la Seconde Guerre mondiale parmi certains manifestants, et bien que l’une des principales raisons du sous-financement profond du système scolaire français soit la forte augmentation des dépenses militaires françaises, dirigées en grande partie contre la Fédération de Russie (le budget militaire, hors pensions militaires, a connu une hausse de plus de 24 milliards d'euros entre 2022 et 2027, passant de 39,2 à 63,4 milliards d'euros), les événements actuels dans les rues de France n’auront aucun impact sur la politique étrangère de Paris vis-à-vis du conflit en Ukraine. Seule l’élection d’un nouveau président français, qui sera avant tout guidé par les intérêts de son pays, pourrait changer le vecteur des relations franco-russes. Politnavigator : La police agit très durement — quel tollé on verrait dans les médias occidentaux si on agissait ainsi contre les « libéraux » en Russie ! Est-ce qu’on voit encore et toujours la politique des deux poids, deux mesures ? Oleg Nesterenko : La répression policière lors des manifestations soulève à nouveau la question du deux poids, deux mesures. L’Occident collectif, et la France ne fait certainement pas exception, est synonyme de deux poids deux mesures. Leur politique étrangère, inchangée depuis des siècles, repose encore sur le vieux principe romain de « Ce qui est permis à Jupiter n'est pas permis au bœuf ». Seuls des bouleversements politiques et économiques nationaux d'une ampleur considérable seraient susceptibles de contraindre à une réévaluation de cette politique de la permissivité et à une réorientation face au monde non occidental. Et, compte tenu des réalités géopolitiques et économiques contemporaines, ces temps semblent être au coin de la rue. L’article Causes et conséquences des manifestations de masse en France : Crise systémique de l’éducation et perspectives politiques est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Clerk-to-Parliament Djietror resurrects debate and justifies why new Chamber for MPs is important
items.description: The Clerk-to-Parliament, Ebenezer Ahumah Djietror, has reiterated the need for a review of Parliament’s infrastructure needs to enhance legislative business. He said the Legislature needed a new Chamber, adequate workspaces and meeting facilities to accommodate Members of Parliament (MPs) and staff of the Parliamentary Service. He explained that the existing facilities were inadequate to accommodate MPs and support the effective discharge of their constitutional responsibilities, with the shortage of meeting spaces forcing some caucuses to seek alternative venues. “We do not have a Chamber with complementary facilities that will enable us to discharge our duties properly. We should be able to have enough workspace, meeting areas, division rooms, ministers’ lobbies, caucus lobbies so that when there are issues, a caucus will not necessarily have to file out and travel all the way to Job 600,” he said. Addressing a workshop for members of the Parliamentary Press Corps (PPC) a in Accra, Mr Djietror said the existing caucus meeting rooms could accommodate only about 30 to 35 people, making it difficult for larger groups of MPs to meet effectively. “Look at the Majority Caucus and where in Job 600 will you have space for them to meet and yet you are to meet as a caucus, as it is part of the rules of engagement” he said. The two-day event, sponsored by Parliament, was meant to build the capacity of PPC members in the execution of the mandate as parliamentary reporters. Mr Djietror said the infrastructure constraints were particularly concerning as Parliament prepared for budget consideration, when committees would invite ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to provide information on their programmes and expenditure. He explained that committee meetings could involve several officials from each agency, in addition to committee members, putting further pressure on the limited space available. Accurate reportage The Majority Leader, James Agalga, said Parliament’s image should be enhanced through improved performance, accountability and responsible journalism rather than the suppression of criticism. He called on parliamentary journalists to ensure that their reports were accurate, balanced and contextual. Mr Agalga said the media played an indispensable role in helping the public understand Parliament’s work and its contribution to democratic governance. Commendation The Chief Information Officer of Parliament, Dr Kate Addo, commended the media for its contribution to bringing Parliament closer to the people since the inception of the Fourth Republic. She said reports and documentaries produced by journalists had helped the public to understand the work of the Legislature. The Director of the Media Relations Department, David S. Damoah, urged members of the PPC to uphold accuracy, fairness, balance and responsibility in their coverage of parliamentary proceedings to strengthen public trust in the legislature. The Dean of the Parliamentary Press Corps, Simon Agianab, urged parliamentary journalists to uphold professionalism, accuracy and constitutional awareness in their coverage of Parliament.

items.title: IGP to CPs: Policing must change, get closer to the people
items.description: By Evelyn Usman The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, has challenged Commissioners of Police, CPs, across the country to strengthen their engagement with communities under their jurisdictions, insisting that effective policing depends on public relations, regular contact and mutual understanding between the police and the people. The IGP gave the charge during a virtual meeting with the CPs, where he urged them to assess their relationship with the communities they police and determine whether they had earned sufficient trust to engage residents, particularly during periods of tension. Recalling the #EndSARS protests, Disu cited instances in which some Divisional Police Officers (DPOs) came out of their stations to engage protesters, with some persuaded to leave, as an example of how direct engagement could help manage tensions. The IGP described the officers involved as examples of policemen who had established sufficient presence and relationship within their communities to influence public behaviour during a volatile period. He said: “When these youths went to some police stations, some divisional police officers came out and addressed them and told them to go back, and they listened to them.Those are the police officers who have been on ground. “All of you should ask yourself a question: Can you stay in front of the people you police and talk to them and get the right response?” he asked. The IGP also questioned whether the police commanders had sufficiently endeared themselves to the communities they serve. “Have you endeared yourself to the people? I know those who are doing it among you, have you endeared yourself to the people?” “Policing must change,” he declared. “Policing is not gragra .Policing is public relations. Policing is contact with the people you are policing. Policing is agreement between you and the people you are policing.” Reactions from some social media handles on the video, suggested that the IGP’s directive had renewed attention on the need for police commanders to prioritise community engagement, maintain regular contact with residents and ensure that officers remain accessible to the people they serve Some commentators also stressed the importance of public cooperation in policing, particularly in intelligence gathering, crime prevention and the management of situations that could escalate into conflict. Others noted that the responsibility of the police extends beyond maintaining law and order to building trust and fostering constructive relationships with the communities they are mandated to protect. The post IGP to CPs: Policing must change, get closer to the people appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GIDEON OLAJIDE (1930-2026): A tribute to a beloved church father
items.description: By Prof. Jacob Kehinde Olupona The passing of the Rt. Revd. Gideon Isaac Oladipo Olajide, retired Bishop of the Diocese of Ibadan (Anglican Communion), marks the end of an era for the Church of Nigeria. I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family and to the whole Anglican Communion in Nigeria. Baba, as many of us lovingly called him, was a towering figure in the Church. In many respects, he was perhaps the last bishop of his generation. His passing calls us to two things: to celebrate a life well lived and to reflect solemnly on what he gave to the Anglican Church we hold so dear. Above all, it calls us to remember the movement he quietly championed, which many regard as a clarion call for a holiness church and true evangelism, if not for a reform of the Church itself. Baba hailed from Igbemo-Ekiti, Ekiti State, Nigeria. He was consecrated Bishop of the Ilesa Diocese in 1981 and later translated to Ibadan in 1988 as Bishop of the Ibadan Diocese. Rt. Revd. Olajide belonged to a generation of priests educated and trained to change the Church’s rhythm. He originally came from the Ondo-Benin Diocese, once one of the largest dioceses in the Nigerian Church, before it was divided into Ondo and Benin, and later into many more dioceses That single diocese’s growth into many is itself a picture of what his generation accomplished: a Church that multiplied because its clergy took the work of the Gospel seriously. It was an era when the Anglican Church clamoured for educated clergy, degree-holding priests who could lead the Church in faithfulness and service. Nigeria was changing quickly, and the Church was exploring many ideas, including the possibility of a Church Union. Universities were rising, a new educated laity was emerging, and the Church needed priests who could speak to the pew’s current realities. This was made possible by the leadership of clerics such as Bishop S. O. Odutola, Bishop of Ibadan in 1960, and others in the Eastern part of the country, such as Bishop Gideon Otubelu and Archbishop Benjamin Nwankiti. For me, Bishop Odutola remains one of the most educated bishops in the history of the Nigerian Church and a man with a broad vision for its future. Baba Olajide was one of the fruits of that vision. Bishop Kale in Lagos and several others of blessed memory played critical roles in the emergence of the Nigerian Anglican renaissance. Rt. Revd. Olajide’s life history has been fairly well documented by Professor Olutayo Adesina of the University of Ibadan in his book Right Reverend Gideon Isaac Olajide: The Making of the People’s Bishop (2000). Those interested in the journey of his life up to his Episcopate in Ibadan may obtain copies to read. Baba attended the famous Christ School, Ado-Ekiti. From there he trained for the priesthood in Ibadan. After his ordination, he served in Iruekpen in today’s Edo State and then as a parish priest in Benin City. Those early years of parish ministry, far from the centres of power, formed the cleric in him. He learned the Church from the ground up: its congregants, its struggles, and its hopes. That grounding never left him, even as he rose to the Church’s highest offices. He later travelled abroad for further studies and returned home better equipped for the work ahead. The church tradition of doing curacy abroad, particularly in the Anglican dioceses in England, was common. My own father also served in Kingswood Parish, Bristol, UK. Many of his classmates did the same. The overseas short-term visit was part of an exchange program because the English church also sent priests to Nigeria and Africa, and some were instrumental in church development projects, education, hospitals, and so on. On his return, Baba Olajide was appointed Warden of a hall of residence and later Assistant Deputy Registrar at the University of Ife (later Obafemi Awolowo University), where he was joined by the Revd. J.B.P. Lafinhan, a Baptist and a distinguished cleric like Baba himself. The University of Ife was fortunate to have him as Warden for many years. On several occasions, he also served as acting chaplain of All Souls’ Chapel, bringing the same pastoral warmth to the chapel that he brought to the hall. He was a reformist priest and administrator. Many who passed through Ife in those years carried his influence into their careers, families, and churches. Baba was later appointed Provost of the Cathedral Church of St. James, Ibadan, under the Most Revd. T. O. Olufosoye, then Bishop. He was consecrated Bishop of Ilesha in 1981 and in 1988, translated to the Diocese of Ibadan, where he served until his retirement in March 2000. As a Bishop, he raised others who would become the future of the Anglican Church in Nigeria. In Ilesha, he ordained young men who later became bishops. One of them, the late Bishop Jacob Ajetunmobi, served as his chaplain and later became the first Bishop of Ibadan South. In the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s, Baba led a critical mass of priests within the Anglican Church, giving rise to a deep form of evangelical and charismatic Christianity often associated with the Scripture Union (SU). This was no small thing, as it brought new fervour to Anglican worship, renewed seriousness about personal faith, and a hunger for the Scriptures among young people across Western Nigeria. Some saw it as a challenge to old ways; in truth, it was a call back to the heart of the Gospel. Baba was a thoroughly evangelical cleric, and his passion for the Good News never waned. He championed the ordination and appointment of several bishops in south-western Nigeria. Many of his mentees rose to the episcopate, among them Bishop Elijah Ogundana, Archbishop Ephraim Ademowo, Archbishop Akinfemiwa, a recently retired Bishop of Ibadan, Archbishop Michael Akinyemi, Archbishop Adebayo Akinde, Archbishop Abiodun Olaoye, Bishop Matthew Osunade. His Episcopacy in Ibadan between 1988 and 2000 saw further reforms. He played a pivotal role in establishing new dioceses, including the Ife Diocese (1990), Oke Osun Diocese (1993), Ibadan North (1998), and Ibadan South (1999). His period was an era of church growth. I was fairly close to Baba, first as a young scholar at the University of Ife, and later as a professor in the United States who travelled home often and never took my eyes off the life of the Church, particularly the Anglican Church. He was my father’s contemporary in the old Diocese of Ibadan, and he knew our family well. He was also one of the Church’s fathers who constantly asked me why I had not been ordained a priest, a question I have always understood as an expression of his care for me and his hopes for the Church. One memorable act truly endeared him to me. In 1999, I sent my last two children to spend their holiday in Nigeria. Realising they had not yet been confirmed, I asked their uncle in Ibadan, Mr. Tunde Olupona, a barrister, to find a church preparing candidates for confirmation so they could register and be confirmed before returning to the United States. I still don’t know how Baba heard about it, but he did something I considered remarkable. He arranged a special confirmation for our two young children in the bishop’s chapel in Ibadan. He and the newly appointed Bishop of Ibadan South, Rt. Revd. Ajetunmobi, conducted the service at the Bishop’s Court, Ibadan. They were joined by our uncle, later Bishop, the Venerable Titus Bamidele Fajemirokun. News of the special confirmation spread, and the children’s relatives in Nigeria attended in large numbers. When the children returned to the United States, they told their friends, with some pride, how famous their father was in Nigeria. I sat them down and corrected them: the service was held primarily in honour of their grandfather, who had served the Church faithfully. I have reflected on that act for years, and I do so again now that Baba Olajide has gone to rest. It revealed the mind of a dignified man of God: sincere, committed to his faith, attentive to individuals, and generous with his love throughout his life. In his lifetime, Baba honoured those who deserved it, and he kept the faith to the end. God blessed him with a long life, long enough to see several of his mentees become influential and charismatic men within the Anglican Communion. It was a long journey, and he walked it faithfully and triumphantly to its close. Once again, my condolences to the family of Baba Gideon Olajide and to the Church of God he leaves behind. As we mourn his passing, we give thanks for his life and pray that God will renew His Church and restore true faith, love, and peace among us. May the soul of Baba Gideon Oladipo Olajide rest in perfect peace. Jacob K. Olupona FNAL, NNOM, D.D. Edinburgh Harvard University, Cambridge, USA The post GIDEON OLAJIDE (1930-2026): A tribute to a beloved church father appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Droits humains : la FEDE lance un prix pour étudiants au Maroc
items.description: Vingt ans après son implantation dans le Royaume, la Fédération européenne des écoles institue un prix dédié aux droits humains, avec le Conseil de l’Europe. Sport, justice et lutte contre la corruption : trois thèmes guideront les projets des étudiants. C’est à Mohammedia que la Fédération européenne des écoles (FEDE) a donné, mercredi dernier, le coup d’envoi de la première édition du Prix spécial des droits humains au Maroc. Montée avec le Bureau du Conseil de l’Europe dans le Royaume, l’opération a été dévoilée devant les établissements marocains membres du réseau, réunis pour marquer les vingt ans de présence de la fédération dans le pays. Le dispositif s’adresse à tous les étudiants des écoles affiliées à la FEDE au Maroc, qu’ils portent leur projet seuls ou en équipe. L’objectif : transformer les principes des droits humains en réalisations tangibles. Selon la fédération, les candidatures devront partir des réalités locales et reposer sur un travail de terrain. Trois thématiques pour cette première édition Le premier axe met en regard sport et droits humains, à l’approche de la Coupe du monde de football 2030. Les projets pourront y aborder l’inclusion, la lutte contre les discriminations ou encore la protection des enfants dans la pratique sportive. Le deuxième axe touche à la justice : accès au droit et protection des personnes vulnérables y occupent le centre de la réflexion. Le troisième croise lutte contre la corruption et droits humains, autour des notions de transparence, d’intégrité et d’égalité dans l’accès aux droits. Un lancement porté par le Conseil de l’Europe Le prix a été officiellement lancé par Javier Gomez Prieto, chef du Bureau du Conseil de l’Europe au Maroc. À cette occasion, il a également présenté les actions que l’organisation conduit dans le Royaume. Pour les écoles participantes, l’initiative doit prolonger l’enseignement académique par un engagement citoyen et mettre en lumière les démarches des étudiants, toutes filières confondues. Claude Vivier Le Got, présidente de la FEDE, a résumé l’esprit de la démarche : « Notre mission ne s’arrête pas à la formation de professionnels compétents. » Elle entend faire de l’engagement citoyen une dimension à part entière du cursus dans les écoles marocaines du réseau. Vingt ans de présence, 70 000 diplômés La rencontre a aussi donné lieu à un état des lieux de deux décennies d’activité dans le Royaume. D’après la FEDE, 70 000 diplômés ont été formés durant cette période avec l’appui de ses établissements membres. Un bureau local assure par ailleurs un suivi de proximité auprès des écoles du réseau. Sa présidente a insisté sur la continuité d’un partenariat bâti avec les établissements marocains, et sur la nécessité d’ajuster l’accompagnement aux besoins du pays. L’évolution des formations et leur adéquation avec les compétences attendues par les entreprises ont ainsi figuré parmi les principaux points débattus. Une séance conduite par Xavier Paroutaud, directeur pédagogique de la FEDE, a porté sur l’évolution des diplômes, des référentiels et des modalités d’évaluation. Selon lui, plusieurs cursus ont été remaniés pour suivre les mutations des métiers et rendre les parcours de formation plus cohérents. Il a également souligné l’importance d’épauler les écoles dans la mise en œuvre de ces changements. Créée en 1963, la FEDE est une organisation internationale non gouvernementale qui rassemble plus de 560 établissements d’enseignement supérieur et de formation professionnelle répartis dans 46 pays. Elle bénéficie du statut participatif auprès du Conseil de l’Europe et du statut consultatif auprès de la Francophonie, et entretient un partenariat officiel avec l’UNESCO. The post Droits humains : la FEDE lance un prix pour étudiants au Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Rosso : réunion de la commission régionale des urgences pour prévenir une éventuelle crue du fleuve Sénégal
items.description: La commission régionale des urgences de la wilaya du Trarza, a tenu une réunion présidée par le wali Ahmedna Ould Sid Ebba, afin d'examiner les mesures préventives à prendre en prévision d'une éventuelle crue du fleuve Sénégal. La réunion a porté sur les moyens de renforcer la préparation et la coordination entre les autorités administratives, les services techniques et les forces de sécurité, afin de garantir une intervention rapide et d’assurer la protection des habitants et de leurs biens si la situation venait à évoluer. Le wali a souligné la nécessité de surveiller le niveau du fleuve, de renforcer la vigilance et de prendre les mesures nécessaires en temps opportun, tout en informant la population des dernières informations confirmées par les canaux officiels. Il a ajouté que cette réunion s’inscrivait dans le cadre des efforts visant à renforcer la préparation locale et à suivre l’évolution de la situation du fleuve, grâce à la coordination des interventions des autorités administratives, des services techniques et des forces de sécurité, ainsi que la mise en place des mesures préventives nécessaires pour limiter les risques potentiels et protéger la population et ses biens.

items.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a ‘racist terrorist attack’, Macron says
items.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has labelled a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which killed one person and injured five others “a racist terrorist attack”. Macron said the attack was a “turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation” – the first time there has ever been a random racial killing like this. The attack unfolded over some 15 minutes with the attacker opening fire from his car – first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La Verrière – appearing to target people of migrant origin. He was subsequently arrested. Three of those injured, including a 12-year-old girl, remain in a serious condition. Visiting the scene of the attack in Trappes, Macron said people had been targeted for their skin colour or religion and urged the public not to give an inch in the face of what he called “ideologies taking root”. The exact motive remains unclear, but the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT) said the incident appeared to be “murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. The suspect has been named in French media as Kevin T who, according to PNAT, had four previous convictions which had been “automatically expunged”. The 39-year-old was known to police but not to France’s intelligence services, local media report. He was not on a list of individuals considered to be a serious threat to French security, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office told BFMTV. A member of the suspect’s “immediate family circle” was also taken into custody on Friday, it added. The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that “an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered” on Friday morning. The gunman drove through several neighbourhoods in a grey Renault Clio, according to witnesses. Rabeh said he had “fired randomly” with the seeming intent of causing “as many casualties as possible… he wanted to cause carnage”, he said. The mayor said people had been targeted at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground in Trappes before the attacker had driven on to nearby La Verrière. A police union official said the suspect had been detained in La Verrière on the main N10 road that runs through the town.The mother of the injured 12-year-old told French broadcaster RTL her daughter suffered eight gunshot wounds and needed surgery. “How could anyone do this to a child?” she asked. The mother said her daughter had been wearing a headscarf and questioned whether this was why she was attacked. “She’s a child who was born in France, in Trappes. She has the right to live in France, to make her life in France,” she added. The attacker reportedly travelled down a main road, shooting intermittently out of his car window. A local police chief told BFMTV that the suspect had used “an older-style semi-automatic weapon” with bursts of fire. Le Parisien reports that the gun dated back to World War Two. PNAT said its investigation also includes “possession of a Category A weapon” – which includes military-grade weapons or weapons capable of firing in bursts. The anti-terrorist office also said its investigation is looking into “conspiracy with a terrorist group for the purpose of preparing crimes against persons”.

items.title: La Steg rétablit l’accès à son site web après une interruption préventive
items.description: La Société tunisienne de l'électricité et du gaz (Steg) a annoncé le rétablissement de son site officiel ainsi que la reprise de ses services en ligne. Cette réactivation intervient après une coupure temporaire décidée à titre conservatoire par l'entreprise publique, qui avait procédé à la désactivation préventive de sa plateforme numérique à la suite du signalement, à l'échelle internationale, d'une vulnérabilité informatique globale. La mesure visait à protéger le système d'information de l'établissement et à prévenir tout risque d'exploitation malveillante de cette faille de sécurité, selon un premier communiqué publié hier par la Steg. Après la mise en place des correctifs requis et le rétablissement des conditions de sécurité nécessaires, la plateforme est de nouveau opérationnelle, indique la même source, qui précise toutefois que l'accès au site web et à ses prestations numériques est pour le momenr restreint et accessible uniquement depuis le territoire national. Y. N. L’article La Steg rétablit l'accès à son site web après une interruption préventive est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .
